body:
The PR view (#174), built slice by slice on `t3/build-pr-view-feature` and merged into `main` here as one unit.

**This PR is also the recorded fixture.** It analyses itself: v1 is recorded at its current head, slice 4's code is pushed to it, and v2 is recorded at the new head (#178, "The recording"). Merge it with a merge commit only, so the analysed SHAs stay reachable from `main`.

## Slices
- [x] 1. The analysis crate: schema, validator, migrations and the agent's tools (#175, merged via #188)
- [x] 2. The analysis run and its API (#176, merged via #189)

Each slice's issue holds its test evidence and the decisions made on gaps in the spec.

issues.title: PR view spec
issues.body:
The implementation-ready spec for the first shippable **PR view**, assembled from the decisions on [Wayfinder: PR view spec](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/142). This issue holds what every slice shares: the problem, the principles, the build order and the rules. Each build slice is a sub-issue with its own decisions, sources and tests. A slice links the map tickets it comes from; where a slice and a ticket differ, the slice is the later word (see "Decided while assembling").

## Problem Statement

An engineer reviewing a large pull request (hundreds of files, several services) can't see what it does to the system from GitHub's file list. They review by asking where data flows, where the external connections are, the order of actions, and which modules and services the change touches, then drill into a part or a connection for short answers, down to exact lines. Today that takes hours of reading, and nothing shows the unchanged system around the change or checks the PR's stated purpose against its code.

## Solution

beghu shows a PR as a graph an agent built from its code, at `/:owner/:repo/pull/:number/view`. The engineer's own agent does the analysis: beghu serves it instructions, a schema and a validator through an **analysis run**, started from the PR panel's **Analyse** button (a copied prompt) or the **beghu CLI**, and takes the upload. beghu never reads code. The view draws the whole system with the change in it, opens parts in place down to files and claims, reads the PR through its **purposes** in a walkthrough, and puts **conflicts** (stated vs code, purpose vs purpose, purpose vs code outside the diff) side by side with no verdict. Every statement is a **claim** that ends at evidence.

## User stories

1. As a reviewer, I want to click Analyse on a PR and paste the prompt into my agent, so that I get an analysis without installing anything.
2. As a reviewer who automates, I want `beghu analyse owner/repo#N` in my agent's flow, so that every PR I file is analysed.
3. As a reviewer, I want the PR panel to tell me whether an analysis exists, is running, was refused or is behind the PR's head, so that I know what I'm looking at.
4. As a reviewer, I want to see the whole system with the changed parts in one group and the unchanged in another, so that I see the change's reach.
5. As a reviewer, I want to open a part in place, down to its modules and files, without losing where I was, so that I can drill and come back.
6. As a reviewer, I want every answer to end at exact lines at the PR's SHAs, so that I can check it.
7. As a reviewer, I want the PR's purposes walked through in a few sentences each, with the code that serves each one drawn and the rest folded away, so that a huge PR stays digestible.
8. As a reviewer, I want the description's claims checked against the code, and a purpose's rules checked against all of head, shown as two facts side by side, so that I find what the PR says but doesn't do.
9. As a reviewer, I want lenses for modules, data flow, external connections and order of actions, so that I can ask each of my questions of the same graph.
10. As a reviewer, I want a second explorer, Path, that walks connections column by column, so that I can follow one thread through a graph too big to see at once.
11. As a reviewer on a phone, I want to pinch a map and pick from a list, so that I can read a PR away from my desk.
12. As a reviewer, I want a re-analysis to keep names, IDs and colours where the code didn't change, and to show what it renamed, merged or corrected and why, so that I can compare.
13. As the only person who sees my analyses, I want them private to my account and deleted with it.

## Principles (binding on every slice)

The settled brief's principles ([the settled brief](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/142#issuecomment-6921640431)) as amended on the map:

1. **A claim with evidence is the building block.** Evidence is exact code lines (side, path, range, snippet), or, for the purpose view only, a verbatim quote of the PR description or an issue the run served. A claim the agent can't back is "couldn't determine", with where it looked.
2. **Code is the only source for the code view.** The purpose view may also draw on the description and served issues, each claim naming its source. The validator enforces the split (`claim.stated-only`).
3. **Facts only: observe and report.** No comparing, judging or recommending. The validator flags judging and comparing words. Placement follows structure, never likeness.
4. **Separation of concerns is visible, not judged:** responsibilities and facets on every part.
5. **Rebuilt from code on every run, stored in beghu, never in the repo.** A run starts from the previous run's IDs and vocabulary, never its claims, and every previous ID that disappears is accounted for in `carried`, with evidence.
6. **One graph, several lenses, one canvas.** Parts open in place along one hierarchy: system → part → module → file → lines.
7. **The stated order** (boundary crossings; new and removed parts; changed responsibilities or facets; edits inside parts) survives as the folded "All changes, by kind". The panel leads with the walkthrough.
8. **Depth is pulled, not pushed.** Answers at most two sentences against fixed question lists; a walk is 2–3 sentences; drilling gives the next level.
9. **Facets are discovered per repo,** their vocabulary carried between runs, their colours derived from IDs.
10. **"Changed" means the part's own code changed.** People, external systems and stores the PR merely starts using stay unchanged; their new lines carry the change.
11. **Lines are per interaction:** one `call` per (caller, callee responsibility), each with a call-site claim. Importing is not a line.

## How it fits together

| Piece | Where |
|---|---|
| Schema, validator, migrations, merge | `crates/analysis` (no I/O), WASM build `crates/analysis-wasm` → `validate.mjs`, `merge.mjs` |
| The agent's instructions | `crates/analysis/instructions/ANALYSIS.md` |
| Runs and analyses | `crates/analysis-db`, one `analyses.db` per account beside its mirror; token and CLI credential hashes in `control.db` |
| Run API | `/api/runs/{token}/…`, started by `POST /api/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/runs` or `POST /api/cli/runs` |
| The view's data | `GET /api/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/analysis` (graph), `…/analysis/{id}/v{version}/claims` |
| The CLI | `crates/cli` (`beghu`); the server becomes `beghu-server` |
| The view | `web/src/pr-view/`, its own chunk; layout in `web/src/pr-view/layout/` |
| Fixtures | `fixtures/pr-view/` (recorded analyses of beghu's own PR, cases), a tiler for perf sizes |

## Build order

1. [The analysis crate: schema, validator, migrations and the agent's tools](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/175)
2. [The analysis run and its API](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/176)
3. [The PR panel's Analyse button](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/177) — the PR holding 1–3 then analyses itself: the owner records **v1**
4. [Fixtures: the recorded analysis, fixture PRs, the tiler and the server gates](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/178) — pushed to the same PR; the owner records **v2**, then it merges
5. [The beghu CLI](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/179) — independent of the view; alongside 6–12
6. [Our layout](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/180) — alongside 5 and 7
7. [The PR view: route, loading and panel](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/181) — alongside 5 and 6
8. [The canvas](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/182) — after 6 and 7
9. [Purposes: the walkthrough, conflicts and the fold plan](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/183) — after 8
10. [Path](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/184) — after 9
11. [The order of actions lens](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/185) — after 8; alongside 9 and 10
12. [The phone and touch](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/186) — last

## Rules for every slice

- `AGENTS.md` and `CONTEXT.md` bind as for v1: StyleX and token colours in both themes, the first-load budget (the view's chunk never loads with the list: `browser.cold.pr-view-modules` = 0), perf gates with owner-reviewed budgets, SQL only in database crates, Fake GitHub modelling GitHub, tests through public seams, the review rules (named error classes, an `Errored` boundary above every async read, writes that roll back).
- **AGENTS.md changes, each in the slice that makes it true:** `crates/analysis-db` joins the database crates (slice 2); the CLI's tests join "Tests go through public seams" (slice 5); the layout rules test joins "The allowed exceptions" (slice 6); the WebKit project joins the browser suite's notes (slice 12); `beghu-server` replaces the server's name wherever it's named (slice 5).
- **Glossary:** use `CONTEXT.md`'s PR view terms (Analysis, Analysis run, Claim, Purpose, Part, Line, Area, Seam hint, Candidate, Partly drawn part) and the ones this spec adds: Canvas, Path, Fold plan, Group, Rest block, Trunk, Conflict.
- **Check UI changes on the recorded analysis** (`./dev-ctl start`, `./dev-ctl login tomsj`) and as `ilze-k` (no analysis), in both themes.

## Checks against real GitHub before the slices that need them

- **Slice 3:** whether `pull_requests: read` covers `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/commits` without `contents: read`. If not, "behind" reads "outdated" with no count.
- **Slice 5:** whether a macOS binary cross-built on Linux runs on an M-series Mac after a `curl` download. If not, a macOS CI job builds it.

## Decided while assembling

The map left these to the spec, or two tickets met in a gap. Each is decided in its slice; the owner should look them over.

- **The spec's form:** this issue plus one sub-issue per slice (the owner's choice; one issue would pass GitHub's 65,536-character limit).
- **Routes:** the view at `/:owner/:repo/pull/:number/view`; runs started at `POST /api/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/runs` and ended at `DELETE …/run`; the CLI's `POST /api/cli/runs`; the device flow at `POST /api/cli/login` and `…/poll` (slices 2, 5, 7).
- **Copy again** (slice 3): the server stores only the token's hash, so the browser that started a run keeps its prompt in `localStorage` until the run ends; another browser gets "Copy a new link", which supersedes the run.
- **The mirror's head SHA** arrives by a `.rebuild.sql` migration (a re-import); "N behind" is counted when the PR's detail is read and cached per (analysed head, current head) (slice 3).
- **The schema starts at version 1** with `drawn: {partial, folders}` in it, since nothing has shipped; one generated `schema.ts`, copied into `web/src/bindings/` (slice 1).
- **The split tools' shapes:** fragments and merge output carry `hints`; `merge --finish` strips resolved ones; `validate.mjs` takes `--split` and `--previous` (slice 1).
- **`Beghu-Snippets: checked | not-checked`,** an upload header, drives the "checked by the uploader's tool" label (slice 2).
- **One live event, `analysis`,** for run state changes and accepted uploads (slice 2).
- **Lines carry no text labels at any level**, only counts, since our layout leaves no room for them ("Extend our layout to nested blocks" put counts on the line) (slice 8).
- **A line that isn't confirmed is dotted,** because dashed already means it crosses a boundary (slice 8).
- **Lines are purple** (quiet and strong) per "Extend our layout to nested blocks", superseding the legend ticket's "lines always use the change colours"; the legend's line rows follow (slice 8).
- **Stores sit in the outside column** with external systems, where the `outside-*` boxes group them (slice 8).
- **Defaults:** lens Modules and services, Show the whole system, Colour by the change, own-part Boxes by Folder, outside Boxes by the required `outside-*` facet, no Outlines (slice 8).
- **Keys:** the canvas's keys are touchpoints in a new `canvas` area of `keys.ts`, rebindable; Backspace folds the innermost open frame around the selection and selects it, since there are no zoom scenes to go out of (slice 8).
- **Facet value colours:** 12 categorical tokens, picked by a stable hash of facet and value IDs with probing on collision; purpose colours: 8 categorical tokens by reading order (slices 8, 9).
- **"Rest block"** names the canvas's muted, dashed, unopenable blocks ("5 other people", "6 folders not drawn"), because `CONTEXT.md` already uses Stub for an issue in an unsynced repo; the layout's points on a frame's edge are **ports** (slices 6, 8, 9).
- **"Code view at ‹part›"** leaves the purpose fold for layout A opened down to that part, with "← Back to ‹purpose›" restoring the fold as it was (slice 9).
- **The legend's wording**, row by row (slice 8), and the order lens's rows (slice 11).
- **"Since the last analysis"** gains a third group, "No longer drawn", for `carried` entries with `cause: scope` (slice 7).
- **The boundary panel:** a boundary gets a panel listing what crosses it (slice 8).
- **Recording:** slices 1–3 are one PR; v1 is recorded at its head when slice 3 works, slice 4's code is pushed to the same PR, and v2 is recorded there (slice 4).
- **The tiled perf PRs** live in the fixture's `AdvanGrid/beghu` repo, numbered above the real ones (slice 4).

## Out of Scope

- **beghu running the agent itself** (server-side jobs, code access, a model bill). A separate effort.
- **Sharing analyses between teammates.** Each is private to its uploader.
- **Analysis history.** Only the latest per account and PR.
- **Per-user customisation of the analysis.**
- **Free-form questions.** The question lists stay fixed.
- **Questions to the attached agent, and PR comments from the view.** The run stays attached and pins its head so these can come later.
- **beghu's internal agents** cloning repos themselves.
- **A coarse or cheaper analysis mode.** One shape, one depth.
- **Native Windows CLI** (WSL covers it), and CLI distribution through crates.io, Homebrew or GitHub Releases.
- **A "too big to draw" mode.** Path serves that need.

## Further Notes

- **Prototypes** (throwaway branches, all under `web/prototype-pr-view/` unless noted): [`t3/pr-view-diagrams`](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/tree/t3/pr-view-diagrams) (2bd1e46, the original: `ANALYSIS.md`, `schema.ts`, `validate.ts`, the panel), [`t3/pr-view-top-level-variants`](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/tree/t3/pr-view-top-level-variants) (2053e39: layout A, Path as G), [`t3/pr-view-scenarios`](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/tree/t3/pr-view-scenarios) (5f76636), [`t3/pr-view-legend`](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/tree/t3/pr-view-legend) (592a480), [`t3/pr-view-mobile`](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/tree/t3/pr-view-mobile) (17c0ffa), [`t3/pr-view-walkthrough`](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/tree/t3/pr-view-walkthrough) (6049795), [`t3/pr-view-purpose-canvas`](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/tree/t3/pr-view-purpose-canvas) (91bfecc), [`t3/pr-view-own-layout`](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/tree/t3/pr-view-own-layout) (d866b88), [`t3/pr-view-nested-layout`](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/tree/t3/pr-view-nested-layout) (86d3a41), [`t3/pr-view-one-canvas`](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/tree/t3/pr-view-one-canvas) (3b97517), [`t3/pr-view-panel-prototype`](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/tree/t3/pr-view-panel-prototype) (195dd97, `web/src/PrototypePrAnalysis.tsx`).
- **Research:** [`docs/research/pr-view-layout.md`](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/blob/15a46d138b0b8899f0923b6d3f9d84cbd8ae8d4b/docs/research/pr-view-layout.md) (why not ELK).
- **Real data:** the #2627 analysis (AdvanGrid/advangrid) quotes private code and is never committed; it stays in the prototype's gitignored `data/` on the owner's machine. The committed recordings of beghu's own PR replace it for everything in the repo.

issues.title: Fixtures: the recorded analysis, fixture PRs, the tiler and the server gates
issues.body:
Part of [PR view spec](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/174). Build order: **4 of 12**, after "The PR panel's Analyse button". Everything that tests or gates the view is built on this.

## What this builds

The recorded analysis of beghu's own PR, the fixture repo and PRs that serve it, the tools that put analyses into a stack, the tiler for perf sizes, the coverage test, and the CI job that keeps the recordings honest.

Sources: [Design the synthetic analysis and fixture PRs that tests and perf gates use](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/167), [Decide how the analysis's prompt, schema and validator are versioned](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/168), [Decide how the PR view loads its analysis, and its perf gates](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/152), [Choose how the PR view lays out its graph](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/162).

## The recording

- **The PR that builds slices 1–3 analyses itself.** Once slice 3 works, the owner runs a real agent on it through `./dev-ctl start --github` against the dev App: **v1** at that head. This slice's code is pushed to the same PR, and **v2** is recorded at the new head, so v2's `carried` entries and "Since the last analysis" are real. Then the recordings are committed and the PR merges (merge commits only, so the analysed SHAs stay reachable from `main`).
- **`./dev-ctl analysis record <run>`** saves the run's pinned `pr.json` and its accepted analysis, untouched, as `fixtures/pr-view/beghu-<n>/pr-v1.json`, `analysis-v1.json`, `pr-v2.json`, `analysis-v2.json`. They count toward the fixture generator's hash.
- beghu's repo is public, so quoting its code leaks nothing.
- **Never hand-edited, never rewritten.** A recording keeps the schema version it was written in. Every upload path migrates it through the server's own migrations, so every schema change is tested against a real older analysis.
- **Re-recording is the owner's call,** when the prompt or agent rules have moved enough that the recording no longer shows what agents write. It replaces v1 and v2 together and reruns the coverage test; a case the new recording covers is deleted.

## The fixture and Fake GitHub

- At every scale the fixture gains an **`AdvanGrid/beghu` repo** with its own installation, as `twin_repo` has. It holds the recorded PR and its linked issues at their real numbers, nothing renamed, so the analysis stays byte for byte what the agent wrote.
- Fake GitHub serves the recorded PR's real title, body, SHAs and file list from `pr-v*.json`, at v1's head. The control call from slice 2 moves it to v2's head, which is how v2 and "N commits behind" are set up.

## How analyses reach a stack

- **Always through the analysis run** (start, fetch to pin, upload), for recordings, tiled copies and cases alike. `analyses.db` is never seeded.
- `./dev-ctl start` and `./dev-ctl reset` upload v1, move the head, then upload v2, **as `tomsj` only**. `reset` empties every `analyses.db` first. Every other fixture user has no analysis, so `./dev-ctl login ilze-k` shows `NoAnalysis`.
- **`./dev-ctl analyse <owner/repo#n> [--as USER] [--version 1|2|tiled-1x|tiled-3x|<case>]`** uploads on demand.
- **Server tests:** the `common` harness starts with an empty `analyses.db`; a helper uploads a chosen version through the run. Tests opt in.

## The tiler (perf sizes)

- A deterministic, cached Rust tool (a `tools/` binary or a fixture-crate binary, beside the fixture generator) that calls the `analysis` crate as a library: it migrates the real analysis, then tiles it to **#2627's shape** (about 76 top-level parts, 167 lines, ~1,250 claims) and to **3×**. It prefixes each copy's paths and IDs, wires a few lines between copies, and writes a matching file list and `pr.json`.
- The results are two synthetic PRs in the **50k** fixture's `AdvanGrid/beghu` repo, numbered above the real ones. Prose and evidence keep real lengths; the uploads pass the server's checks (the server never reads code).
- **The perf stack** uploads both tiled analyses as its user once, untimed, before any gate runs. Its brotli 9 cost is paid at start, not skipped.
- **The layout suite's committed synthetic graph** (slice 6) is cut from the same output: the drawable graph only (nodes, lines, groups, facet values), committed at 1× and 3×, regenerated by the tiler.

## Coverage

- **A coverage test** reads the committed analyses and fails if the real one and the hand-written cases together miss any required feature: `when` build and test, `uses`, `data.direction` (each value), `drawn` partial, sub-purposes, a rule that holds and one that breaks, a cause shared by two conflicts, each conflict kind, `unclaimed`, served issues, `carried` of each kind, chapters, claims with evidence of each kind.
- Each gap gets a small, complete, hand-written analysis of the same recorded PR in `fixtures/pr-view/cases/<feature>.json`, quoting real code so it passes the same snippet check. Cases are written only after the real analysis exists, and only for what it lacks. `422` inputs are never committed; tests build them next to their assertions.

## CI

A job runs the **full validator, snippet check included,** on every committed recording and case against the real commits (fetched by SHA), on their migrated form, and checks those commits are still reachable from `main`.

## Server perf gates

With the tiled analyses on the 50k stack, the server suite gains, each calibrated from a measured run (+15% timings, +5% bytes, exact counts) with a reason in `perf-budgets.toml`:

| Gate | Measures |
|---|---|
| `server.analysis.ms` / `.kb` / `.scan` | the graph answer: time, brotli bytes as sent, full scans (0) |
| `server.analysis-claims.ms` / `.kb` / `.scan` | the claims answer, the same three |

The two `.kb` gates exceed the 14 KB first flight on purpose, and their reasons say why: the view is its own route, never a first page, and the graph is the smallest answer that can draw.

## Done when

v1 and v2 are committed, the coverage test passes with whatever cases it needed, `./dev-ctl start` shows `tomsj` an analysis of the recorded PR in the panel, the CI job is green, and the server gates are calibrated.

## Evidence: slice 4 (PR #192, head `10add27`)

v1 is recorded and committed. v2 is still to come: it gets recorded on #191's new head after this PR merges into the feature branch, which completes this issue's "Done when".

### `./dev-ctl start` gives `tomsj` the recorded analysis
These screenshots come from a 1k fixture stack after `./dev-ctl reset`. Fake GitHub serves #191 from `pr-v1.json`, and v1 is uploaded through an analysis run as `tomsj` only.

| `tomsj` (light) | `tomsj` (dark) |
|---|---|
| ![tomsj light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/pr-view-evidence/178/tomsj-light.png) | ![tomsj dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/pr-view-evidence/178/tomsj-dark.png) |

The popover shows the recorded analysis: c7842a6, 120 parts · 5 purposes · 3 conflicts.
![popover](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/pr-view-evidence/178/tomsj-popover.png)

`ilze-k` has no analysis, so the button reads **Analyse**:
![ilze-k](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/pr-view-evidence/178/ilze-k-light.png)

The screenshots were taken with this script: [shots.mjs](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/blob/pr-view-evidence/178/shots.mjs).

### The recording
- `fixtures/pr-view/beghu-191/analysis-v1.json` is the agent's upload, byte for byte (sha256 `0f537083…cf47`). `pr-v1.json` is the PR as the run pinned it ([hashes](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/blob/pr-view-evidence/178/recording-sha256.txt)).
- The server now keeps every accepted upload's body (analysis-db migration 0003, `upload_gz`). `./dev-ctl analysis record <run>` writes that body out untouched. It reads the database through SQLite's online backup, and refuses runs on any repo other than `AdvanGrid/beghu`.

### Checks
- **[`analysis-fixtures check`](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/blob/pr-view-evidence/178/fixtures-check.txt):** this is CI's `pr-view-fixtures` job, run locally. It runs the full validator, snippet check included, against the real commits. v1 and all four cases are ok with **0 warnings**; v1 had 18 judging-word warnings before this slice.
- **[Coverage test](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/blob/pr-view-evidence/178/coverage.txt):** it passes. The five features only v2 can supply are listed as waiting on it: `since-last-analysis` and `carried-{renamed,merged,split,dropped}`. The test fails if v2 lands without them.
- **[`analysis` and `analysis-fixtures` test suites](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/blob/pr-view-evidence/178/analysis-tests.txt):** all pass. They include the judging-word probes.
- **[The tile test](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/blob/pr-view-evidence/178/tile.txt):** it passes.
- **CI on #192:** green on each earlier head, including the full browser suite. The perf comment shows the six new server gates passing.

### The tile (#2627's shape)

| | Parts | Top-level lines (distinct pairs) | Edges | Claims | Parts with no line |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1× (#9001) | 76 | 167 | 281 | 1,287 | 0 |
| 3× (#9003) | 228 | 503 | 845 | 3,861 | 0 |

### Server gates

| Gate | Measured | Max |
|---|---|---|
| `server.analysis.ms` | 2.82 | 3.3 |
| `server.analysis.kb` (brotli) | 74.36 | 78.1 |
| `server.analysis.scan` | 0 | 0 |
| `server.analysis-claims.ms` | 3.02 | 3.5 |
| `server.analysis-claims.kb` (brotli) | 122.64 | 128.8 |
| `server.analysis-claims.scan` | 0 | 0 |

The timings are the median of three `--full` runs at load 36–42, +15%. The best run was a low outlier that a fourth run missed by 4×. CI measured about 0.6 ms on both. `server.facets.scan` goes from 37693 to 37696; it's itemised in its reason and confirmed with `BEGHU_SCAN_STEPS=1`: the new repo, and the recorded PR's author in the author and assignee lists.

### Decisions made in this slice
- **What gets recorded.** `record` saves the upload exactly as accepted. The server now stores it, so analyses accepted before this change can't be recorded.
- **The fixture repo.** `AdvanGrid/beghu` is added to every scale under its own installation (41000003). Its items are dated 400 days back, so the default list's top doesn't change. The tile PRs, #9001 and #9003, are in every scale.
- **What Fake GitHub models.**
  - **Base SHAs:** Fake GitHub stores a PR's base SHA, and `/push` takes `base_sha`. A PR's first commit keeps its parent when the base moves, as on GitHub.
  - **Switching versions:** going from one version to another is symmetric. Going back deletes the later version's comments, matched by author and body through an outside edit.
  - **Inactive webhooks:** a change made while webhooks are off is never delivered, as with an inactive webhook on GitHub. This fixed an intermittent 401 after sign-in.
- **Cases.** A case named `cases/<f>.after-v1.json` is validated and uploaded as a later analysis after v1. Only such a case can supply `carried`.
- **Judging words.** A capitalised or joined word is a name only if the analysis writes it as code somewhere. "Well-designed", "best-in-class" and "less-than-ideal" are flagged.
- **Tests on two installations.** The reconcile tests run on two installations, except four that count one installation's reads, which say so. A new test checks that both installations are probed, polled and swept.
- **Not built yet.** Slice 6's committed layout graph isn't cut yet: its format belongs to slice 6.

issues.body:
Part of [PR view spec](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/174). Build order: **1 of 12**, first. Nothing else can start before the schema exists.

## What this builds

The no-I/O Rust crate `crates/analysis`, which every producer and consumer of an analysis shares, its WASM build (`validate.mjs`, `merge.mjs`), and the instructions the analysis run serves. The server, the beghu CLI, CI, `./dev-ctl`, the test harness and the tiler all call this crate. None of them carries its own copy of a rule.

Sources: [Design the analysis link and its API](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/149), [Decide which agents the instructions target, and how a large PR is split](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/151), [Decide what the agent must draw in the graph, unchanged parts included](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/156), [Decide what a grouping node the agent invents must carry](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/147), [Keep scenarios short enough to follow](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/146), [Decide what an upload must keep from the previous analysis](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/150), [Decide the purpose and conflict data the agent produces](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/161), [Decide how the analysis's prompt, schema and validator are versioned](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/168), [Decide what the PR view's explorers share, and what Clusters needs to ship](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/170) §7. Prototype starting points: `schema.ts`, `ANALYSIS.md` and `validate.ts` in `web/prototype-pr-view/` at [2bd1e46](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/tree/2bd1e46/web/prototype-pr-view), with chapters from [`t3/pr-view-scenarios` 5f76636](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/tree/5f76636/web/prototype-pr-view) and the purpose shape in [`purpose.ts` on `t3/pr-view-walkthrough`](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/blob/6049795e9ebb49491b9bf49aab78925b6b1ed36d/web/prototype-pr-view/purpose.ts). Where these differ from the decisions below, the decisions win.

## The crate

- **No I/O.** Types, checks, the report, the merge and the migrations. File contents come through a reader trait the caller supplies (the server passes none, the CLI passes one over the two checkouts, the WASM build one over `node:fs`).
- **No SQL**, so it isn't a database crate. It depends on `serde`, `serde_json` and `ts-rs`, and nothing that does I/O.
- **The Rust types are the schema.** `ts-rs` generates them, doc comments included, into one file, `crates/analysis/generated/schema.ts`, which `cargo test` regenerates and which is committed. The run serves that file as `schema.ts`, and `cargo test` also copies it to `web/src/bindings/analysis.ts` for the web app. The doc comments are part of the agent's instructions, as the prototype's field comments were. Write them for an agent.
- **Production starts at schema version 1.** The prototype's analyses never shipped and aren't migrated. Version 1 already has everything below, `drawn.folders` included (§7 of the explorers ticket said "the next bump"; there is none yet).

## Schema version 1

Field names are camelCase in JSON. Every `claims` field is a list of claim IDs.

**Top level:** `version`, `pr`, `coverage`, `walk` (the PR's), `nodes`, `edges`, `boundaries`, `scenarios`, `facets`, `purposes`, `conflicts`, `causes`, `unclaimed`, `unbacked` (present exactly when `purposes` is empty), `carried`, `claims`.

**`pr`:** repo, number, title, url, author, description (verbatim), `baseSha` (the merge base the agent computed with `git merge-base <base tip> <head>`), `headSha`, stats.

**`coverage`:** summary; skipped (generated files, lockfiles, fixtures) with reasons and counts; notes on limits; `references: [{ref, how: "own-tools" | "unreached"}]` for linked references the run didn't serve.

**`Node`:** `id` (from paths), `kind` (`system | service | app | library | module | store | external | actor`), `parent`, `name`, `paths`, `summary`, `change` (`added | modified | removed | unchanged`), `changeSummary` (also the panel's "What it now does"), `responsibilities: [{id, text, change, claims}]`, `facets: FacetAssignment[]`, `zone`, `questions: [{question, answer, claims}]`, `files: [{path, status, added, removed, generated, summary}]`, optional `drawn: {partial: true, folders: number}` (an unchanged part opened only along a path; `folders` is the part's total folder count), optional `walk`, optional `built: [{kind: decision | constraint | assumption, text, claims}]` (changed parts only).

**`FacetAssignment`:** `{facet, values: [{value, claims}], was?: valueId[]}`. Every value of a `multi` facet carries its own claims, unordered, with no "main" value.

**`Edge`** (a line): `id`, `from`, `to`, `kind` (`call | data | event`; `dependency` is gone), `when` (`runtime | build | test`, required), `uses` (the callee's responsibility ID, required on `call`), `label`, optional `data: {what, direction: forward | back | both}` (required on `data` and `event`; on `call` only when domain data crosses), `mode` (`sync | async | n/a`), `change`, `boundaries`, `facets`, `questions`, `claims`, optional `occurs` (prose "when": "on every probe start"), optional `walk`, `neededBy: [{text, node?, purpose?}]` (required wherever the line has a walk).

**`boundaries`:** `{id, kind: trust | process | network | tenant, name, claims}`.

**`scenarios`:** `{id, title, trigger, steps: [{from, to, action, data?, edge?, change, claims}], chapters: [{title, from}]}`. `from` is the chapter's first step's 0-based index; steps stay one flat list.

**`facets`:** `{id, name, question, appliesTo: node | edge, multi, values: [{id, label, prefix, description}]}`, each with an `unknown` value. Grouping facets: `outside-*` (2–3, for external systems and stores; "what it does for this system" required) and one `inside-*` ("What part of the product is it for?", multi, required on every top-level own part).

**Purposes** (one flat list, array order is reading order, top-level purposes first):
```ts
interface Purpose {
  id: string;            // path-like slug: "purpose:tenant-isolation", "purpose:tenant-isolation/role-check"
  name: string;
  parent?: string;       // two levels at most
  kind: "feature" | "process" | "security" | "fix" | "groundwork" | "chore";
  walk: Walk;
  stops: { ref: string; line: string }[];          // ordered: sub-purposes, parts at any level, lines
  serves: { node: string; role: string; claims: string[] }[];   // the deepest part that serves it
  carries: { edge: string; why: string; claims: string[] }[];   // lines its flow passes along
  rules?: Rule[];
}
interface Walk { intro: string; journey: string; destination: string; claims: string[] }
interface Rule {
  id: string; text: string; scope: string; sources: string[];   // claim IDs
  checked: { searched: string; found: number; holds: number; breaks: number; undetermined: number };
}
```

**Conflicts and causes:**
```ts
interface Conflict {
  id: string;
  kind: "stated-code" | "purpose-purpose" | "purpose-outside";
  question: string;            // both sides answer it; no verdict
  cause?: string;              // a causes[] id
  a: Side; b: Side;            // exactly two
  rule?: string;               // purpose-outside: the rule it breaks
  touches: { purposes: string[]; nodes: string[]; edges: string[] };
}
interface Side {
  who: "description" | "issue" | "code" | "outside" | "purpose";
  purpose?: string;
  says: string;                // a few words, shown on the card
  text: string;                // the whole fact
  claims: string[];
  sites?: { claims: string[]; more: number };  // purpose-outside: the first 20 breaks, then a count
}
// causes: { id, text, claims }[]   (code evidence required)
// unclaimed: { node, reason }[]    (changed leaf parts no purpose serves)
// unbacked?: string                (one or two sentences; only when purposes is empty)
```

**`carried`:** `{kind: renamed | merged | split | dropped, was, now: string[], cause: code | correction | scope, reason, claims}`. Covers node, edge, facet, facet value and purpose (and sub-purpose) IDs. Conflicts, causes, scenarios and chapters don't carry.

**Claims:** `{id, text, status: supported | undetermined, evidence: Evidence[], lookedAt?}`, IDs `c1…`.
```ts
type Evidence =
  | { kind: "code"; side: "base" | "head"; path: string; start: number; end: number; note: string; snippet: string }
  | { kind: "description"; quote: string; note: string }
  | { kind: "issue"; repo: string; number: number; quote: string; note: string };
```
The panel's "backed", "stated, not found in code" and "code" are derived from the evidence kinds; the agent never writes them.

## The validator

One report format everywhere: `{errors: [{path, rule, message}], warnings: [...]}`, `path` a JSON pointer, `rule` a fixed ID. The validator never exits before its output is written (the prototype's piped output was truncated, [#143](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/143)).

**It migrates first.** Given an older version it runs the migration chain, adds a `schema.migrated` warning (from vN to vM) and checks the migrated form. A version newer than its own is `version.unknown`.

**Checks with no reader (the server runs these):**
- Shape and references: every ID referenced exists; enums; required fields by kind.
- Every prototype `validate.ts` check that doesn't need the code, each given a rule ID: "changed" normalisation (people, externals and stores never "modified" for being newly used), lines per interaction, every changed file placed in exactly one node, judging and comparing words (warnings, not errors), and the rest.
- Chapters ([#146](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/146)): error on missing chapters, a first chapter not at step 0, chapters out of order or off the steps; warn on a chapter over 6 steps; judging words in titles.
- Grouping ([#147](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/147)): every node but `system`, `external` and `actor` has `paths`; a node with children has a responsibility with claims; a top-level part has no children of top-level kinds; every top-level own part has an `inside-*` value; every value of a multi-valued assignment has a claim.
- Lines ([#156](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/156)): `when` set; `uses` on every `call`, naming a responsibility of `to` or a descendant; `data` on every `data` and `event` line; generic `data.what` ("data", "request") flagged; every line has a claim whose code evidence lies under the `from` node's paths (or, from an external or actor, under the `to` node's: the receiving entry point).
- Principle 2: `claim.stated-only` — only claims behind purposes, roles, walks and conflict sides may rest on description or issue evidence alone.
- Purposes and conflicts ([#161](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/161) §11): `purpose.depth`, `purpose.redundant-member`, `purpose.no-members`, `purpose.stop-not-member`, `walk.required` (the PR, every purpose, every stop, every changed top-level part), `conflict.kind-sides`, `conflict.touches`, `unclaimed.missing`, `unbacked.exact`.
- `carried` against a previous skeleton: given `previous-ids.json` and `vocabulary.json` (the run serves both), every previous ID missing from the analysis needs an entry, else `carry.unaccounted`, naming each missing ID and what it was. Every entry has a `cause` and a claim with evidence.

**Checks with a reader (the CLI and `validate.mjs` run these too):**
- The snippet check: every code evidence's snippet matches its side, path and line range.
- Every `paths` entry exists at base or head.
- `drawn.folders` matches the folder count in the checkout.

**Checks only the server can run** (slice 2 adds them around the validator, with these rule IDs): `evidence.quote-mismatch` (description and issue quotes, word for word, against what the run pinned), `evidence.issue-not-served`, the head SHA against the pinned one, and `carried` against the stored previous analysis.

## The split procedure's tools

- **`split.json`:** `mode: single | split`; `areas: [{id, prefixes, owns: changedFile[], reads: topLevelPart[], estimate, system: bool}]`; `candidates: [{from, to, why}]` (pairs of top-level parts where one might use the other); `purposes: [{id, name, parent?, kind, sources, flow: {entries, path}}]`; `rules: [{purpose, id, text, scope, sources}]`.
- **The split check** (`check-split`): every pinned changed file in exactly one area; every top-level part in exactly one area, changed or system; areas don't overlap; IDs path-derived.
- **A fragment** is a partial analysis plus `hints`: `seam` (a line it expects to cross into another area), `candidate` (each candidate the area owns, drawn as line IDs or rejected with a claim), `purpose` and `rule` (an area can't create a purpose or rule; it hints one).
- **`merge`:** joins fragments, renumbers claims, drops coarse skeleton lines the areas replaced, and writes the merged analysis with its `hints` still on it: every unmatched seam hint, every cross-area line that ends at a parent when a child of it exists in the other area, every unresolved candidate, every purpose and rule hint.
- The seam pass resolves each hint (draws the line, deepens it, adds or folds the purpose, or rejects with a claim). The validator refuses any unresolved hint (`hint.unresolved`), and `merge --finish` strips the resolved ones. An upload carrying `hints` fails the shape check.

## The WASM build

- A `crates/analysis-wasm` cdylib over the crate, built to `wasm32-unknown-unknown` with `wasm-bindgen`, inlined as base64 into two single Node files with no npm install: `validate.mjs` (`node validate.mjs <analysis> <base dir> <head dir>`, plus `--split <split.json>` and `--previous <dir>`) and `merge.mjs` (`node merge.mjs <fragments…>`, `--finish`).
- CI and the `Dockerfile` add the target and `wasm-bindgen-cli`; `wasm-bindgen` goes through `cargo deny` and `cargo vet`. The server serves the two files built from its own commit. `./dev-ctl` rebuilds them when the crate changes.

## Migrations

- Each step is a function `vN → vN+1` over `serde_json::Value`; the chain ends by deserialising into the current types. Old type definitions aren't kept.
- A step that renames IDs returns a rename map (old → new, with the step), which the server stores as `migratedIds`. Steps should avoid renaming IDs.
- A step may reshape data but never edit quoted code or line ranges.

**Guards, tests through the crate's entry points:**
1. The generated `schema.ts` records its version and a hash of itself with comments stripped. The test fails if the shape changed but `version` didn't, and says to add a migration step. Doc-comment edits don't trip it.
2. The chain has exactly `version − 1` steps, from v1, with no gaps.
3. Every committed recording (slice 4) migrates and validates, and its evidence is the same before and after.

## The instructions (`ANALYSIS.md`)

The production instructions live at `crates/analysis/instructions/ANALYSIS.md`, included in the server at build time. Rewrite the prototype's `ANALYSIS.md` to every decision on the map. The run (slice 2) adds a header. What they must say:

- **Who they're for:** any coding agent with a shell and git, in capability words ("native subagent orchestration", "native workflow orchestration"), never product names. Node and orchestration are optional and the text branches on them. Smaller models aren't promised to work.
- **The checkout:** base and head at the pinned SHAs, with the harness's native worktree handling, plain git commands as the fallback. Compute the merge base locally. beghu's tools never check out code.
- **The procedure** ([#151](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/151), [#161](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/161) §7): read `previous-ids.json` and `vocabulary.json` first; skeleton (`pr`, facets and vocabulary, boundaries, top-level parts, outside nodes, actors, purposes with flow sketches, rules, candidates; `single` or `split`; areas from the repo's own structure, sized as "what one agent can read and describe in one context", with fixtures, lockfiles and generated files counted cheap); `check-split`; checkpoint (an interactive harness shows the areas and estimate and asks; a non-interactive one proceeds); areas (parallel where the harness orchestrates, else in sequence with fragments on disk), each given its slice of the previous IDs; merge; rule checks, one per rule; the seam pass and scenarios; validate; upload.
- **What to draw:** the settled brief's agent rules ([the settled brief](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/142#issuecomment-6921640431), "Settled for the analysis agent"), as amended: no grouping nodes and the `inside-*` facet (#147's rule text, word for word); every direct connection at head between top-level parts, unchanged ones included, one `call` per (caller, callee responsibility), imports are search aids, never lines; `when` and `data` as above; a call-site claim on every line; a suspected connection drawn with an `undetermined` claim and `lookedAt`; unchanged parts coarse, opened only along a path (`drawn`); every hop of a scenario at its deepest node, cut into chapters, one per moment (a person acts, a write is picked up later, a deploy stage ends).
- **Purposes:** names and order from the description, the served issues and the code; issues the run didn't serve may be read with the agent's own tools but are never evidence, and go in `coverage.references`; a stated promise no code serves is a stated-vs-code conflict with an `undetermined` code side; rules checked against all of head, the scope as written, one hop deep; one conflict per broken rule, with the first 20 sites; causes only with code evidence; how purpose-vs-purpose conflicts are found (every part serving two or more purposes); the fallback (`purposes: []`, `unbacked`, every changed leaf in `unclaimed`).
- **Writing:** observe and report only, no recommendations; answers at most two sentences, each with claims, against the fixed question list per element type (carried over from the prototype); a walk is one paragraph of 2–3 sentences, intro → journey → destination; a role is one line; a conflict's question has no verdict and `says` is a few words; quote the description and issues verbatim.
- **Carrying over:** reuse previous IDs; declare every one that goes in `carried`, with evidence.
- **Every limit** (slice 2's sizes and file cap) and the cost line: large PRs are split and can take an hour.

## Done when

- `cargo test -p analysis` passes the three guards and a test per rule ID, each on a small hand-written analysis edited next to its assertion.
- `validate.mjs` and `merge.mjs` build in CI and the `Dockerfile`, and a CI step runs both on a hand-written analysis under plain Node.
- `cargo deny` and `cargo vet` pass with `wasm-bindgen`.

## Test evidence: branch `t3/pr-view-175-analysis-crate` at 157970e

There's no visual change in this slice, so the evidence is test and tool output.

**`cargo test -p analysis`: 112 tests pass** ([full log](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/blob/0ed3aa679e5c6952bb6017c8a6a06ba9d422ccd2/175/cargo-test.log)). They cover:
- one test per rule ID, each editing the hand-written sample next to its assertion, plus a meta-test that every rule ID has one
- the three guards:
  - the schema hash, over the upload's types only, with doc comments ignored
  - the migration chain's length
  - recordings migrate with their evidence unchanged
- the merge, `--finish` and the split check, including every malformed position the merge and validator must survive without a panic

**`validate.mjs` / `merge.mjs` under plain Node** (v26, no npm install; [log](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/blob/0ed3aa679e5c6952bb6017c8a6a06ba9d422ccd2/175/node-tools.log)):
1. The sample validates clean, with the snippet, path and tracked-folder checks.
2. A broken copy reports `line.uses` and `evidence.snippet` as errors and `words.judging` as a warning, each at an exact JSON pointer.
3. The split check passes on the skeleton.
4. `merge.mjs --split` joins the skeleton and two areas into 9 nodes, 4 lines and 17 claims, leaving seam, candidate, purpose and deepen hints.
5. `--finish` refuses the 4 unresolved hints with `hint.unresolved`.
6. An untracked `node_modules` in head doesn't change `drawn.folders`.
7. An 8 MB input's report piped through `cat` arrives whole.

**Other checks:**
- Passing: fmt, clippy (workspace, `-D warnings -D clippy::disallowed_methods`), `cargo deny --locked check` (`url` bumped to 2.5.9 for RUSTSEC-2026-0592), `cargo vet --locked`, zizmor, actionlint, web typecheck and lint.
- Not passing: some server suites (`reconcile`, `relationship_writes`, `accounts`) flake under a load average of about 70–90. `reconcile` fails the same way on the base commit, and the server doesn't depend on this crate.

### The owner's decisions on gaps in this spec
- `drawn.folders` counts folders at any depth that hold at least one file git tracks at head.
- `validate.mjs` takes the changed files from an optional `--pr pr.json`, and `--split` runs only the split check.
- Area IDs equal one of their prefixes without the slash. A root prefix is refused (`split.prefix`).
- In `split.json`, `estimate` and `sources` are free text, and `mode` is removed: a `split.json` exists only in a split run. Single mode writes none and skips check-split.
- The merge infers which skeleton lines an area replaced. When an area and the skeleton write the same ID, the area wins silently; when two areas do, the merge warns (`merge.duplicate`).
- `merge.mjs --split split.json` turns every candidate no fragment answered with a `candidate` hint into an unresolved hint. A drawn line doesn't count as an answer.
- Seam hints take an optional `uses`, and only a line with that `uses` answers them.
- Purposes and rules settled by the skeleton or `split.json` are an area's to write. Anything else an area writes becomes a `purpose` or `rule` hint.
- `carried.was` names a facet value as `<facet>/<value>`. Infra, CI and docs are `module` nodes.
- The schema guard hashes only the types reachable from `Analysis`.
- `serde_path_to_error` is allowed as a dependency, for exact error paths.

issues.title: The analysis run and its API
issues.body:
Part of [PR view spec](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/174). Build order: **2 of 12**, after "The analysis crate".

## What this builds

The **analysis run** on the server: starting, pinning, serving the run's files, taking uploads, storing analyses in a per-account `analyses.db`, serving the graph and its claims to the view, and the live event that announces a change. Fake GitHub learns the PR endpoints it needs.

Sources: [Design the analysis link and its API](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/149) (with its amendment), [Decide what an upload must keep from the previous analysis](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/150), [Decide the purpose and conflict data the agent produces](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/161) §3, [Decide how the PR view loads its analysis, and its perf gates](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/152), [Decide how the analysis's prompt, schema and validator are versioned](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/168), [Decide which agents the instructions target, and how a large PR is split](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/151) (the prompt).

## The run

- One agent's session against one PR for one connected account. Producers: the button (slice 3), the beghu CLI (slice 5), later beghu itself. After the start every producer uses the same run API.
- **One live run per account and PR.** Starting a run supersedes the live one.
- **Lifetimes:** a button run unused for 24 h expires; a started run expires after 2 h idle (no authenticated call), and at most 7 days after its start.
- **Revoked** when the user ends it (panel, or `beghu analyse end`), or the account signs out, goes dormant, needs to sign in again, or loses Read on the repo. Every call re-checks these.
- **Refused at start** when the PR has more than 3,000 changed files (`changed_files` from `GET /pulls/{n}`), with a message naming the cap.
- The run outlives its upload: uploads are unlimited within it, and each accepted one replaces the account's latest analysis for that PR.

## Starting

| Call | Who | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/runs` | browser session, as other writes | `201 {run, token, prompt, expiresAt}` |
| `DELETE /api/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/run` | browser session | `204`; ends the live run |
| `POST /api/cli/runs {owner, repo, number}` | CLI credential (`Authorization: Bearer beghu_cli_…`) | `201 {run, token, sizeLine}` |

- **The token** is 256 random bits, URL-safe. Only its SHA-256 is stored, in `control.db` (a request must resolve to an account before beghu knows which account's files to open), beside the run ID and account. A CLI run also requires the CLI's bearer on every run call, so its token alone isn't enough.
- **The prompt** (button runs), word for word:
  > Analyse pull request {owner}/{repo}#{n} ({files} files, +{added} −{removed}) for beghu by fetching your instructions from `https://{host}/api/runs/{token}/instructions` and following them to the end: they say how to check out the code, build and check the analysis, and upload it. Large PRs are split across several agents and can take an hour; treat the link as a password, as it lets anyone holding it act on this PR's analysis until the run ends.

## The run API, under `/api/runs/{token}/`

- **Pinning happens on the first fetch of any run file:** the head SHA, the base branch and its tip SHA, title, body, the changed files from `GET /pulls/{n}/files` (path, previous path, status, counts), and the linked issues, fetched with the account's token. beghu stays off `contents: read` and never reads code. A push during the run never rejects an upload; a newer head needs a new run.
- **Linked issues:** the PR's closing references, plus `#N`, `owner/repo#N` and issue URLs in the description, one hop, and only in repos the account mirrors, read from the mirror with their comments. Every other reference goes in `unreached: [{ref, reason}]`.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `instructions` | `ANALYSIS.md` (slice 1) with a run header: the PR, the pinned SHAs, the size line, every limit, the deploy's build SHA, how to fetch the other files. Button runs name URLs; CLI runs name CLI commands. |
| `pr.json` | the pinned facts: repo, number, title, body, url, author, head SHA, base ref and tip SHA, files, stats, `issues: [{repo, number, title, body, comments}]`, `unreached` |
| `schema.ts` | the generated schema |
| `validate.mjs`, `merge.mjs` | the WASM tools built from the server's commit |
| `previous-ids.json` | nodes `{id}`, edges `{id, from, to}` of the latest analysis, or `404` |
| `vocabulary.json` | facets `{id, name, question, appliesTo, multi, values: [{id, label, prefix, description}]}` and purposes `{id, name, parent}`, no assignments, or `404` |
| `POST analysis` | the upload |
| `POST end` | ends the run |

There is no `previous.json`: the agent mustn't copy claims it hasn't re-checked.

## The upload

- Body: the analysis JSON, optionally `Content-Encoding: gzip`. **8 MB** on the wire, **32 MB** inflated, enforced while inflating.
- Header `Beghu-Snippets: checked | not-checked`. The CLI sets it itself; the instructions tell a button-run agent to send `checked` only after `validate.mjs` passed. The page labels evidence "checked by the uploader's tool" or "not checked".
- **Server checks, in order:** inflate within limits; the validator with no reader (migrating an older version first, slice 1); head SHA against the pinned one; every pinned changed file placed; description and issue quotes word for word against the pinned text (`evidence.quote-mismatch`), issue evidence only from served issues (`evidence.issue-not-served`); `carried` against the stored previous analysis, both migrated first (`carry.unaccounted`). No previous analysis means `carried` must be empty.

| Case | Status | Body |
|---|---|---|
| Accepted | `201` | analysis ID, head SHA, warnings (`schema.migrated` among them) |
| Fails a check | `422` | the error report; nothing stored, the previous stays. After a migration it adds that the schema moved from vN to vM since the run's files were fetched, and to refetch `schema.ts`, `validate.mjs` and the instructions from this run. |
| Newer version than the server's | `422` | rule `version.unknown`, the server's version |
| Too large | `413` | the limits |
| Head isn't the pinned SHA | `409` | the pinned SHA |
| Run expired, revoked or superseded | `410` | why; start a new run |
| Bad token or credential | `401` | |

Warnings never reject. They're stored and returned; the page doesn't show them. A refused upload increments the run's refused count and keeps the last report on the run (the panel shows the count only).

## Storage: `analyses.db`

- **A new schema crate, `crates/analysis-db`**, added to AGENTS.md's database crates, with **in-place migrations only** (no `.rebuild.sql`). One file per account, beside the mirror in the account's directory, deleted with it at dormancy. Not backed up.
- **Runs:** ID, PR, producer (`button | cli | beghu`), state (`waiting | attached | ended`), created, last heard, ended reason, the pinned `pr.json`, refused count, last report.
- **Analyses:** the latest per PR only. ID, PR, schema version, head SHA, merge base, created, run, `Beghu-Snippets`, warnings, summary counts (parts, purposes, conflicts), `migratedIds`, and four blobs.
- **Split once, at upload,** in a blocking task: **the graph** (everything but the claims' bodies; each item keeps its claim IDs and counts, enough for chips such as `code ×n`) and **the claims** (every claim with its evidence). Each is stored at brotli 9 and gzip 9. Brotli 11 is ruled out (over a minute of CPU at the 32 MB cap).

## Serving the view

- **Graph:** `GET /api/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/analysis`, the stored blob as is, chosen by `accept-encoding`. `ETag: "<id>.v<version>"`, `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so a revisit is a `304`. `404` when there is none. The graph names its claims URL and carries the PR's `carried` and `migratedIds` for forwarding.
- **Claims:** `GET /api/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/analysis/{id}/v{version}/claims`, `Cache-Control: immutable`.
- Both are `no-store` for shared caches like every API answer, and private to the account.
- **Migration on read, written back:** any read that needs the analysis (graph, claims, the next upload's check, `previous-ids.json`, `vocabulary.json`) migrates it first if it's behind: inflate, migrate, re-split, recompress both blobs at brotli 9 and gzip 9 in a blocking task, write back in one transaction. A per-analysis lock makes concurrent reads wait on one migration. No sweep at start. The analysis ID stays; the ETag and claims URL change with the version. A migration is not a new analysis and sends no event.
- **A failed migration is a bug:** `500` with its own error class, the stored analysis untouched, the log naming account, PR and versions. Never serve the old shape.

## The live event

The push stream (`crates/server/src/live.rs`) gains one event, `analysis`, with `{repo, number, analysis?: id}`, sent to the account's streams when a run changes state (started, attached, refused, ended, expired) or an upload is accepted. The PR panel refetches the PR's detail on it; the open view compares the ID with its own (slice 7).

## Fake GitHub

Learns, in GitHub's documented shapes and status codes: `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}` (with `changed_files`, `head.sha`, `base.ref`, `base.sha`), `GET …/pulls/{n}/files` (paginated, stopping at 3,000 files as GitHub does) and `GET …/pulls/{n}/commits` (paginated, 250 at most). It **stores a head SHA per PR** (generated PRs derive theirs from the fixture) and a control call moves a PR's head as a push would. The commits list is generated to end at the stored head.

## Tests (`crates/server/tests/`, through HTTP)

Until the recording exists (slice 4), small hand-written analyses, each `422` input built by editing a valid analysis next to its assertion. Cover: start, pin on first fetch, every file served, each upload status, the quote and carried checks, an older-version upload migrated (with a test-only v0 → v1 step, if needed, kept in the test), supersede, expiry and every revocation, the 3,000-file refusal, graph and claims answers with ETag and `304`, the `analysis` event.

## Done when

The checks pass, and a real agent can take a button prompt (copied by hand from the start call) through to an accepted upload on a real PR, with `./dev-ctl start --github` against the dev App.

## Test evidence: branch `t3/pr-view-176-analysis-run` at f2ef06a

**End to end on a `./dev-ctl` stack (1k fixture), driven with curl.**
- The browser starts the run. The agent fetches the run's files with no cookie, validates with the served `validate.mjs` and uploads. The view reads what was stored.
- Log: [e2e-run.log](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/blob/6dd996d731c6c9e09b113f56b98c2d3a46eb14b8/176/e2e-run.log). Script: [e2e-run.sh](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/blob/6dd996d731c6c9e09b113f56b98c2d3a46eb14b8/176/e2e-run.sh).

1. `POST /api/acme/web/pulls/364/runs` answers 201 with the prompt word for word (`(2 files, +22 −0)`, the instructions URL, and the warning to treat the link as a password).
2. All 7 run files answer 200: `instructions` (with the run header: PR, pinned head and base SHAs, size, limits, build), `pr.json` (pinned at the first fetch, with one linked issue served from the mirror), `schema.ts`, `validate.mjs`, `merge.mjs`, `previous-ids.json` and `vocabulary.json`.
3. The served `validate.mjs` reports `0 errors, 0 warnings`.
4. A gzipped upload with `Beghu-Snippets: checked` answers **201**, with the analysis ID, the head SHA and no warnings.
5. The graph comes back brotli-encoded with `ETag "<id>.v1"` and `private, no-cache`; a revisit is a **304**. The envelope carries `claimsUrl` and `migratedIds`, and each claim is cut to evidence counts. The claims answer is `private, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
6. Refusals:

   | Case | Status |
   |---|---|
   | Wrong head | **409**, naming the pinned SHA |
   | Fails a check | **422** (`line.uses` at `/edges/0/uses`) |
   | No `Beghu-Snippets` header | **400** |
   | 9 MB body | **413**, with the limits |
   | Bad token | **401** |

7. Starting a new run answers 201, and the old token then gets **410** `superseded`. `DELETE …/run` answers **204**.
8. The account's live stream hears `event: analysis` four times: started, attached, accepted (carrying the new analysis ID), ended.
9. Disconnect, then sign in again: the graph answers **404** `no_analysis`, because Disconnect deleted the analyses.

The 413 case was sent straight to the server's port. Vite's dev proxy shows the server's early 413 as a 502; production has no Vite in front.

**`cargo test -p beghu --test analysis`: 33 of 33 pass** ([log](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/blob/6dd996d731c6c9e09b113f56b98c2d3a46eb14b8/176/cargo-test.log)). They cover:
- every upload status, and the checks' order
- the quote, issue-not-served and carried checks
- an old version migrated at upload, a migration on read, and a failed migration answering 500 with the stored row untouched
- supersede, both expiries and the 7-day cap from creation
- every revocation (dormant, signed out, sign-in again, lost Read, Disconnect)
- the 3,000-file refusal
- ETag, 304 and the cache headers
- the live event
- races:
  - an upload superseded mid-check
  - two uploads at most doing heavy work at once, even when clients leave
  - a run ended first by another call
  - a sign-in racing a Disconnect
- restarts: expiry timers re-armed, and a Disconnect cut off by a crash finished at startup
- the daily check: retrying a failed lost-Read delete, and pruning runs and tokens

Elsewhere:
- The rest of the workspace passes, apart from suites that flake under heavy host load (`reconcile`, `relationship_writes`, `live`, `relationships`), which pass alone and fail the same way on the base commit.
- fmt, clippy (`-D warnings -D clippy::disallowed_methods`) and the build's SQL check pass.
- `./dev-ctl perf` passed except `browser.filter.ms`, which exceeded its gate once and passed on rerun; this slice doesn't touch the web app.

Four Opus reviews; the last approved with nits only.

### Decisions on gaps in this spec
- **Storage:** `analyses.db` lives at `analyses/<account id>.db`. Mirrors are throwaway caches, and an analysis can't be fetched from GitHub again.
- **Deletion:** analyses are deleted at dormancy, on **Disconnect**, and per repo when the account **loses Read** on it. Disconnect is recorded in `control.db`, so a crash midway is finished at the next start or sign-in. Lost-Read deletes are retried by the daily check.
- **"Signs out":** means signed out of every browser.
- **Lifetimes and tokens:** the 7-day cap counts from the start call. Ended runs' tokens are pruned after 30 days; until then, an old link gets 410 with its reason rather than 401.
- **Upload checks:**
  - Quotes match word for word with runs of whitespace collapsed.
  - A missing or unknown `Beghu-Snippets` answers 400 and isn't counted as refused.
  - The refused count covers 422, 409 and 413.
- **Upload limits:** at most 2 uploads do the inflate, check, split and compress work at once, so concurrent 32 MB uploads can't exhaust memory.
- **Graph shape:** the graph answer is an envelope `{id, version, repo, number, headSha, mergeBase, createdAt, snippets, claimsUrl, migratedIds, analysis}`, with each claim cut to `{id, status, code, description, issue}` counts.
- **Left for later slices:**
  - `POST /api/cli/runs` answers 401 until slice 5 adds the CLI credential.
  - Fake GitHub's `/push` will send `pull_request.synchronize` in slice 3.
  - A real agent taking a button prompt to an accepted upload on a real PR, through `./dev-ctl start --github`, is done with the owner at the v1 recording after slice 3.

issues.title: The PR panel's Analyse button
issues.body:
Part of [PR view spec](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/174). Build order: **3 of 12**, after "The analysis run and its API". When this lands, the owner records v1 of beghu's own PR (see "Fixtures").

## What this builds

The PR panel's **Analyse** split button and its popover, the PR's head SHA in the mirror, and "N commits behind".

Sources: [Prototype the PR panel's side of the PR view](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/169) (and its amendment from [Decide what the beghu CLI is as a product](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/171)). Prototype: [`web/src/PrototypePrAnalysis.tsx` on `t3/pr-view-panel-prototype`](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/blob/195dd97/web/src/PrototypePrAnalysis.tsx), variant B, mounted in the real panel (`?pa=B&pas=…`).

## The button

A split button in the PR panel's status row, just before "Open on GitHub". Its label is the state; the main part does the obvious thing; ▾ always opens the popover.

| State | Label | Main click |
|---|---|---|
| No analysis, no run | Analyse | copies the prompt and starts a run |
| Last run expired, no analysis | Analyse again | the same |
| Run waiting for its agent | ● Waiting for agent (amber, pulsing) | opens the popover |
| Run attached | ● Agent working, or ● CLI working for a CLI run (green, pulsing) | opens the popover |
| Last upload refused | ● Upload refused (red, steady) | opens the popover |
| Analysis at head | PR view (accent) | opens the full-screen view |
| Analysis behind | PR view · N behind (accent), or PR view · outdated | opens the full-screen view |

Until "The PR view: route, loading and panel" lands, the two "PR view" states open the popover instead. Pulsing stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Colours are tokens, each dot paired with its words.

## The popover

- **Analysis** (when there is one): "at ‹short SHA›, ‹age›", the amber "N commits behind" chip when behind, and "N parts · N purposes · N conflicts".
- **Run** (when one is live): three steps (Prompt copied, or Started from CLI; Agent fetched; Uploaded), one status line, **Copy again** (button runs only), **End run**, and a folded "What was copied" with the prompt word for word and the `beghu analyse owner/repo#N` alternative.
  - Waiting: "Waiting for an agent to fetch the instructions. Unused, the link ends in 24 h."
  - Attached: "An agent is working at ‹pinned SHA›, last heard ‹age›. The run ends after 2 h idle."
  - Refused: "Last upload refused: N errors. The agent got the report and can upload again." A count only; the panel never lists errors or warnings.
- **No run:** "Analyse this PR", or "Analyse again" when there's an analysis, with "Copies a prompt for your agent", then a folded line "Or run `beghu analyse owner/repo#N`" with a copy button. An accepted upload replaces the analysis.
- **End run** lives here; the full-screen view doesn't offer it. A CLI run can also end with `beghu analyse end`. Starting a new run supersedes the old one.

## Copy again

The server keeps only the token's hash, so it can't hand the prompt back. The web app keeps the prompt it was given in `localStorage`, keyed by account, PR and run, and deletes it when the run ends, expires or is superseded. **Copy again** copies it. In a browser that doesn't hold it, the button reads **Copy a new link**: it starts a new run (superseding the old) and copies that prompt.

## The data

- **The PR's detail** (`PullDetail`, ts-rs) gains `run?: {producer, state, pinnedSha?, lastHeard?, refused, expiresAt}` and `analysis?: {id, headSha, createdAt, parts, purposes, conflicts, behind?: number | "outdated"}`, read from the account's `analyses.db`. The `analysis` live event (slice 2) refetches it.
- **The mirror gains the PR's head SHA:** a mirror-db migration `…_pr_head_sha.rebuild.sql` adds `head_sha` to PRs, filled by the import and kept current from `pull_request` webhooks and reconciliation. A rebuild re-imports, which is how the mirror gains columns.
- **"N behind"** is the analysed head's position in the PR's commit list (`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/commits`), counted when the PR's detail is read and the mirror's head differs from the analysed head, then cached in `analyses.db` by (analysed head, current head), so one GitHub call per new head. Unreachable from the list (force-pushed away) reads "outdated".
- **Check before building this:** whether `pull_requests: read` covers `/pulls/{n}/commits` without `contents: read`, against the dev App ("What only real GitHub can show"). If it doesn't, skip the call and the label is always "PR view · outdated" when the heads differ.

## Tests

- **Server:** the PR detail's `run` and `analysis` in each state, set up through the run API; `behind` through Fake GitHub's control call that moves a PR's head; the start and end calls.
- **Browser** (`web/e2e/`): each label from its state, the popover's three shapes, Copy (clipboard), Copy again and Copy a new link, End run, the live change from Waiting to Agent working to PR view when an upload lands. Both themes.

## Done when

The checks pass and the owner can start a run from beghu's own PR on the dev App and watch it reach "PR view".
