issues.title: The beghu CLI
issues.body:
Part of [PR view spec](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/174). Build order: **5 of 12**, after "Fixtures" (its tests run on the recorded PR). It touches none of the view, so it can be built alongside slices 6–12.

## What this builds

The **beghu CLI** (`crates/cli`, binary `beghu`): sign-in, the analysis commands, distribution from each deployment, self-update, and the server's side of all of it. The server crate and binary are renamed `beghu-server`.

Sources: [Decide what the beghu CLI is as a product](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/171), [Design the analysis link and its API](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/149) (credentials), [Decide how the analysis's prompt, schema and validator are versioned](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/168) (`MIN_CLI`), [Decide which agents the instructions target, and how a large PR is split](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/151) (`analyse` and its subcommands).

## Naming

- The server crate and binary become **`beghu-server`**: the `Dockerfile` (`/app/beghu-server`, the entrypoint), CI, `./dev-ctl` and `docs/deploy.md`.
- The CLI is `crates/cli`, building **`beghu`**. Both depend on the `analysis` crate.

## Hosts

- The CLI talks to any beghu deployment. It defaults to the hosted one; `beghu login --host URL` adds another.
- Credentials are per host. One host is active (the last logged in to); `--host` on any call overrides it.

## Signing in

- **`beghu login [--host URL] [--no-browser] [--name NAME]`:** beghu's own device flow, never GitHub's, and beghu never receives a GitHub token.
  1. `POST /api/cli/login {name}` answers `{device, code, url, interval, expiresIn}`: `device` is a secret the CLI keeps; `code` is a short code for a person (8 characters, no look-alikes); `url` is `https://{host}/cli/login?code=…`.
  2. Locally the CLI opens `url`. Over SSH or with `--no-browser` it prints the URL and the code.
  3. The CLI polls `POST /api/cli/login/poll {device}` at `interval` until approved (`200 {token, account}`), denied or expired (`410`). The code lives 10 minutes.
- **`/cli/login`** is an app route needing a signed-in session: it takes the code from the URL or as typed, shows the account (with several accounts in one browser, you choose it there) and the machine name, with Approve and Deny.
- **The token:** `beghu_cli_` then 256 random bits, so secret scanners recognise it. Only its SHA-256 is stored, in `control.db`, with the account, name, created and last used. It can only start runs and act within them.
- **Lifetime:** expires after **90 days unused**, no absolute cap. Dies with the account at dormancy. Signing out in the browser doesn't revoke it.
- **The setup page** gains "CLI sign-ins": name (`--name`, the hostname by default), created, last used, Revoke, plus the install line and a link to `/cli`. Revoking takes effect on the next call (`401`); the CLI prints "signed out on the server; run `beghu login`" and deletes its entry.

## On the machine

- `$XDG_STATE_HOME/beghu/credentials.toml` (`~/.local/state/beghu/…`) on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/beghu/` on macOS, created `0600`: one entry per host (token, account login, expiry) and the active host. Not `~/.config` (often in git), not an OS keychain (missing over SSH, in containers and CI).
- `BEGHU_TOKEN` and `BEGHU_HOST` override the file, for CI and containers. It's the same token `beghu login` stored.

## Commands

Account: `beghu login`, `beghu logout [--host URL | --all]` (revokes on the server, then deletes locally), `beghu status` (active host, GitHub account, credential expiry, the CLI's version and build, the host's build and `MIN_CLI`), `beghu update`, `beghu --version` (semver and build SHA).

Analysis, driven by the agent:
- **`beghu analyse <owner/repo#N | PR URL> [--yes] [--max-areas N]`:** starts a run (`POST /api/cli/runs`), superseding any live run for that account and PR. Writes the run's files (instructions, `pr.json`, `schema.ts`, `previous-ids.json`, `vocabulary.json`) to `./.beghu/run-<id>/`, prints the size line, then the instructions with CLI commands in place of URLs. `--yes` skips the checkpoint's question; `--max-areas N` fails fast when the skeleton's split has more.
- `beghu analyse check <file>`: the full native validator, snippet check included, over the checkouts the instructions named.
- `beghu analyse check-split <split.json>`, `beghu analyse merge <fragments…> [--finish]`.
- `beghu analyse upload <file>`: runs `check` first, refuses locally on errors, always gzips, sends `Beghu-Snippets: checked`.
- `beghu analyse end`: ends the run.
- The subcommands find their run from the single `.beghu/run-*` folder in the current directory, so an agent never handles a run ID or credential; `--run <id>` chooses among several.
- Not in v1: listing runs, downloading an analysis.

## Versions and updates

- Every call sends `User-Agent: beghu-cli/<semver>` and `Beghu-Schema: <n>`. The semver is in `crates/cli/Cargo.toml`, bumped by hand when behaviour changes.
- **`MIN_CLI`**, a semver constant in the server with its reason in a comment, bumped with any schema bump and any change whose instructions name a new CLI command. Below it, every call (mid-run included) is `426` with the floor and how to update. A CLI newer than the server gets `409` with the server's version.
- **`beghu update`** downloads the active host's build for this platform, checks its SHA-256 against `manifest.json`, writes it beside itself and renames over (atomic). It installs exactly the host's build, newer or older.
- **On `426`** the CLI updates itself if its file is writable, prints `updated beghu 0.4.1 → 0.5.0 from {host}`, and re-execs the same command once. The run survives. If not writable, it prints the `beghu update` / `install.sh` line and exits non-zero.
- **`409` never updates by itself;** it prints the hint. No background checks, no nag.

## Distribution: each deployment serves its own CLI

- The image carries CLI binaries built from the **same commit** as the server: Linux `x86_64` and `aarch64` (static musl), macOS `aarch64` and `x86_64`. No native Windows; `install.sh` says to use the Linux binary in WSL.
- Built in a new `Dockerfile` stage with `cargo-zigbuild`, so a plain `docker build` makes everything (about 25 MB more image). The publish workflow's SLSA provenance and SBOM cover them; `docs/deploy.md` says how to verify.
- Served at `/cli/{os}-{arch}/beghu`, `/cli/install.sh` and `/cli/manifest.json` (version, build SHA, SHA-256 per binary). `curl -fsSL https://{host}/cli/install.sh | sh` installs to `~/.local/bin` or `$BEGHU_INSTALL_DIR`, no sudo.
- `deploy/smoke.sh` downloads the Linux binary from the running container and runs `beghu --version`.
- **Check first:** a macOS binary cross-built on Linux must run on a real M-series Mac after a `curl` download (zig's linker ad-hoc signs; a `curl` download carries no quarantine flag). If it doesn't, a macOS CI job builds those two and the image copies them in.

## Where engineers meet it

- **`/cli`**, a prerendered public site page in the sitemap (`web/site/`): the install line with `{host}` from `BEGHU_PUBLIC_URL` as `site.rs` does, the WSL note, login (browser or device code), the commands, `BEGHU_TOKEN` for CI, where credentials live, updating, verifying a binary against the image's attestation.
- The setup page's "CLI sign-ins" and the PR panel's popover line (slice 3).

## Development and tests

- **`./dev-ctl cli <args…>`** runs the workspace's `beghu` with `BEGHU_HOST` at the local stack and a credentials file under the stack's data dir. `./dev-ctl login <user>` also signs the CLI in.
- **The CLI is a public seam** (AGENTS.md's "Tests go through public seams" gains it): `crates/cli/tests/` runs the built binary as a subprocess against the server tests' `common` harness and checks stdout, stderr, exit codes and files written:
  - device-code login, approved through the server's HTTP surface;
  - `analyse` → `check` → `upload` on the recorded beghu PR;
  - `426` self-update and retry (the harness serves a newer build's manifest; the test updates a temporary copy of the binary, never `target/`'s);
  - `409`, `401` after a revoke, and `BEGHU_TOKEN`.
- **Browser:** the setup page's "CLI sign-ins" and Revoke, and `/cli/login` Approve and Deny.

## Done when

The checks pass, `docker build` produces an image whose `/cli/install.sh` installs a working `beghu` on Linux, and the macOS check above has passed or its CI job exists.

issues.title: Our layout
issues.body:
Part of [PR view spec](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/174). Build order: **6 of 12**, after "Fixtures" (it needs the committed synthetic graph). It can be built alongside slices 5 and 7.

## What this builds

**Our layout**: one pure TypeScript engine that lays out every drawing in the PR view (the top level, opened blocks, the purpose canvas, the phone map), its rules test, and the `layout` perf suite. ELK is not in production.

Sources: [Prototype our own graph layout for large PRs](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/163), [Extend our layout to nested blocks](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/166), [Choose how the PR view lays out its graph](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/162), [Make the top level readable on a large PR](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/144) (the locked rules), [Decide how the PR view loads its analysis, and its perf gates](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/152). Prototypes: [`own-layout.ts` on `t3/pr-view-own-layout` (d866b88)](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/tree/d866b88/web/prototype-pr-view) and [`nested-layout.ts` and `nested-bench.ts` on `t3/pr-view-nested-layout` (86d3a41)](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/tree/86d3a41/web/prototype-pr-view). Build only the winning path, street routing plus nesting; the prototypes' other variants stay behind.

## Where it runs

- In the browser, on the main thread, inside the PR view's chunk (`web/src/pr-view/layout/`). Synchronous, so opens and folds animate from known positions.
- **A pure function:** graph in, coordinates out, with the previous answer's positions as an optional input. No DOM, no Solid, no StyleX.
- It moves into a Web Worker **only** if a measured run can't meet the layout-time gates below (3× fully open over about 0.5 s on a quiet host).

## Input and output

- **In:** scopes (the drawing, and each open block), each with its parts (ID, size, column: people, changed, unchanged or outside; or for a frame, its own inner layout), the lines rolled up to it (from, to, count, changed, one-way direction for layout), boxes (a column's foldable group frames), the previous positions, and constants (column gap room for counts, 30 px).
- **Out:** every part's and frame's rectangle, every line's route (orthogonal points, exact), the trunks (each a stretch with the lines on it), and per scope its size.

## The method (Highway by street routing)

1. **Columns in the locked order:** people, the changed group, the unchanged group, outside systems. Each group is packed into as few columns as about 1.5 × √parts per column allows. Parts joined by a line never share a column; a line that then points backwards is laid out the other way round. Lines are laid out as if they all ran one way; the arrows keep the real direction.
2. **Rows:** barycentre sweeps order each column.
3. **Parts placed on their own:** each column packed from the top (the changed group and the frame at the top, no empty band) and pulled toward what it connects to by isotonic regression, so nothing overlaps.
4. **Every line routed as one cheapest path:** length, plus 40 px per bend, with a ×0.85 discount on any stretch another line already uses (along a column or up a gutter). Long lines first, then each routed again against the rest. Lines spanning fewer than 3 gutters are local: no discount, and they avoid busy stretches.
5. **Gaps widen only where routes pass,** with 30 px of room per gap for counts; then everything is routed again.
6. **Trunks:** lines on the same stretch merge into one thick stroke, horizontal or vertical. A line joins and leaves trunks freely.
7. **Tracks:** each gutter's verticals sit on tracks ordered to cross least.

**Nesting:**
- A line is drawn in the scope where its two ends part ways, between the two children holding them. Inside each open block on its way down, it runs from the child holding its end to a **port**: a zero-size part on the frame's edge, one per line of the scope above, so a frame's lines fan out from one point on its edge.
- **Three passes:** top down, columns only (which decides each port's edge: left if the line's other end is to the left in the scope above); bottom up, each block's inside (its frame's size and its ports' positions; the scope above then treats the frame as one big part with fixed ports); top down, offsets.
- **Keeping parts in place:** every scope takes the previous answer's positions as heavy anchors, so an open or fold moves only what the changed block pushes (the prototype: 9 of 2,115 parts moved up or down folding one deep block).
- A fully open drawing stays wide (about 6:1 on #2627, because chains inside blocks run left to right). That's accepted; the canvas pans.

**Accepted limits:** a few shallow jogs remain (11 on #2627, about 35 px each) where the 0.85 discount trades a detour for fewer crossings. Lines carry no text labels; counts go on the line where it leaves its part.

## The rules test (a new allowed exception)

`web/src/pr-view/layout/layout.test.ts`, run by `npm run test:lint`. AGENTS.md's "The allowed exceptions" gains it, and its file says why: the rules are geometry no HTTP answer or page shows. On the committed synthetic graph (1× and 3×, top level and fully open, and a fold after an open) it checks:
- no two parts or frames overlap;
- both groups packed from the top;
- every line laid one way;
- no line passes through a part;
- trunks only where lines share a stretch;
- folding back to the previous state restores the previous positions (anchors hold).

## The `layout` perf suite

A new Node suite in `perf/harness` runs the pure engine on the committed synthetic graph (slice 4: #2627's shape and 3×). Gates in `perf-budgets.toml`, calibrated from a measured run on a quiet host, each with a reason:

| Gate | Limit |
|---|---|
| `layout.top.ms`, `layout.open.ms`, `layout.top-3x.ms`, `layout.open-3x.ms` | median of 10, +15% |
| `layout.crossings`, `layout.area` at 1× and 3× | exact |

A change that makes the drawing worse fails CI the way a slower one does. `./dev-ctl perf` runs the suite against local `main` as for the others.

## Done when

The rules test and the suite pass, the budgets are calibrated, and the engine lays out the synthetic graph at 3× fully open within about 0.5 s on a quiet host (or this slice has moved it into a worker).

issues.title: The PR view: route, loading and panel
issues.body:
Part of [PR view spec](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/174). Build order: **7 of 12**, after "Fixtures". It can be built alongside slices 5 and 6. Slices 8–12 build on it.

## What this builds

The PR view's full-screen route and chunk, how it loads the analysis, its top bar and states, the URL and history, and the panel's **reference** content: everything the panel shows that isn't the walkthrough (slice 9 puts the walkthrough on top of it).

Sources: [Decide how the PR view loads its analysis, and its perf gates](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/152), [Prototype the PR panel's side of the PR view](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/169) (top bar, `NoAnalysis`, the newer-analysis pill), [Decide what the PR view's explorers share, and what Clusters needs to ship](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/170) §1–3, [Decide what an upload must keep from the previous analysis](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/150) ("Since the last analysis", forwarding), [Decide how the analysis's prompt, schema and validator are versioned](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/168) (`migratedIds`), [the settled brief](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/142#issuecomment-6921640431) ("Panel"). Prototypes: the panel in [`main.tsx` at 2bd1e46](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/tree/2bd1e46/web/prototype-pr-view) and the mocks in [`PrototypePrAnalysis.tsx`](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/blob/195dd97/web/src/PrototypePrAnalysis.tsx).

## The route and chunk

- **`/:owner/:repo/pull/:number/view`**, full screen, in the app's chrome. The server serves the shell there as for the PR panel's path. The PR panel's "PR view" button links to it.
- **Its own lazy chunk**, `web/src/pr-view/`, never imported statically from the list or panel. The view's code (layout, canvas, Path, panel, sequence view) all lives in it.
- **The router starts the graph fetch alongside the chunk import** (a route preload, as the issue panel's is). A cold open is shell → (chunk ∥ graph) → draw. The claims fetch starts right after the graph arrives.
- **Live facts stay out of the blob:** the current head, "N behind" and the run's state come from the PR's detail (slice 3), fetched as the panel does.

## Loading and failures

Named error classes, thrown from the API layer:
- **The graph fails:** the route's `Errored` boundary replaces the canvas with the error and Retry; the app's chrome stays.
- **`NoAnalysis` (`404`):** a centred empty state: "No analysis of this PR yet", a line saying beghu never reads the code and only you see the result, "Analyse this PR" (the same start as the panel's button) with the CLI alternative. While a run is live, the run's steps and status take the button's place, with "This page fills in when the upload is accepted"; the `analysis` event then loads it.
- **`AnalysisMigrationFailed` (`500`):** the graph's boundary, with its own message.
- **The claims fail:** the drawing, the walkthrough and the counts stay. Every place that shows claim text or evidence (a part's claims, a conflict's sides, a source chip) has its own small boundary: "Couldn't load the evidence" with Retry. One Retry refetches the one claims file. No automatic retry loop.
- **A drill-down that beats the claims** shows a skeleton until they arrive.

## The top bar

"← ‹repo›#‹n›" (back to the PR panel), the PR's title, "analysed at ‹short SHA›, ‹age›", the amber "N commits behind" chip when behind (or "outdated"), and **Analyse again**, or the run's short state while one is live ("● Agent working"), which opens the same popover as the panel's ▾. No End run here. Then the tabs, **Canvas** and **Path** (Path's tab appears with slice 10).

## A newer analysis

On the `analysis` event with an ID other than the one shown, an accent pill: **"A newer analysis is ready · Show it"**. Never swapped by itself. Show it refetches the graph and claims and keeps the reader's place where the selection's ID survives, following the new upload's `carried` (renamed, merged, split) and `migratedIds`; otherwise it goes to the level above.

## State, the URL and history

- **One value for the whole view:** the selection (so the panel never changes on a tab switch), lens, Show, Colour by, Boxes, Outlines and the Lines menu. **Each tab keeps its own:** Canvas its opens, folds, zoom, scroll and ← Back history; Path its columns.
- **The URL**, each parameter written only when not its default: `tab` (`canvas` default, `path`), `sel` as one typed ID (`part:…`, `line:…`, `purpose:…`, `conflict:…`, `step:…`, `group:…`, `unclaimed`), `lens`, `show`, `colour`, `boxes`, `outlines`, `lines`, `scenario` and `chapter` under the order lens, `path=a,b,c` (Path's trail). Canvas's opens are never in the URL: a link opens the canvas in its starting state and opens down to the selection.
- **Desktop history (720 px and wider):** a selection change or a tab switch pushes an entry; opens and folds don't (they stay on the canvas's ← Back and Start over); lens, Show, Colour by, Boxes, Outlines and Lines replace the current entry. Restoring an entry restores the selection and tab, opening down to the selection, not the old opens. The phone's history is slice 12's.
- **Old IDs forward one step,** each with a one-line note: renamed or merged to the new ID; split to the level that holds all the new parts, selected together; dropped to the nearest surviving parent, or the top level, with the reason. An ID renamed by a migration (`migratedIds`) forwards silently. An ID still unknown drops to the PR with "not found in this analysis".

## The panel's reference content

The panel sits beside the canvas (right side, resizable as the issue panel is) and follows the selection. This slice builds what each place shows as reference; slice 9 adds the walkthrough above it and folds this under "Questions, facets, files and evidence" (or "All changes, by kind" at the PR).

- **The PR (nothing selected):** the stated-rule list "All changes, by kind": boundary crossings; new and removed parts; changed responsibilities or facets; edits inside parts. Then the PR description (verbatim, collapsible), coverage (summary, skipped, notes, references read with own tools or unreached, partly drawn parts), the facets found, and **"Since the last analysis"** (folded, when there was a previous analysis): the upload's `carried` grouped as "Code changed", "Corrected" and "No longer drawn" (`cause: scope`), each entry with its reason and claims.
- **A part:** its questions (question → answer → claims → evidence), what it does (responsibilities, each with its change and "used by N parts", worked out from the lines' `uses`), how it's built (facets in words), connections (hidden lines listed faded and labelled, such as "hidden: test"), and its files in a grid (green +, red −, aligned counts, status words). A partly drawn part says under its summary which folders are drawn and why the rest aren't.
- **A line:** each connection's questions, facets, what it carries (`data.what` and direction), when (`when`, `occurs`), mode, boundaries crossed, evidence.
- **A step:** previous and next, and the whole flow.
- **A boundary or group:** see slice 8 (the Group panel).
- **Evidence:** each claim's text, then its evidence: code as a snippet with side, path and lines and a GitHub link at the exact SHA, labelled "checked by the uploader's tool" or "not checked"; description and issue quotes with their source. An undetermined claim reads "couldn't determine", with where it looked.
- **Answers are short:** at most two sentences each; depth is pulled one level at a time.

## Browser perf gates (this slice)

| Gate | Measures |
|---|---|
| `browser.cold.pr-view-modules` | modules from the view's chunk fetched by the list's cold load: **0, exact**. This, not the report-only `browser.first-load.kb`, keeps the route out of first-load JS. |
| `browser.pr-view.kb` | the view's chunk(s), gzip, +5% |

Slice 8 adds the drawing's timings.

## Tests

- **Server:** the shell at the new path.
- **Browser** (`web/e2e/pr-view.spec.ts`, on the recorded analysis as `tomsj`): cold open; `NoAnalysis` as `ilze-k` and the start from it; the graph failing (through Playwright's request routing, since Fake GitHub isn't involved) and Retry; the claims failing locally and one Retry; the newer-analysis pill after an upload through `./dev-ctl analyse`, keeping the place; old-ID forwarding from v1 IDs on v2; every reference place; back and forward through selections. Both themes.

## Done when

The checks pass, the two gates are calibrated, and the view opens on the recorded analysis with a working panel (the canvas may be a placeholder until slice 8).

issues.title: The canvas
issues.body:
Part of [PR view spec](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/174). Build order: **8 of 12**, after "Our layout" and "The PR view: route, loading and panel".

## What this builds

**The canvas**: the one drawing of the code view, in the Canvas tab. Layout A's columns, opening in place, the lenses and toolbar, hover cards, trunks, the legend, groups, partly drawn parts, and the drawing's perf gates. Purposes on the canvas are slice 9; the order lens is slice 11; the phone is slice 12.

Sources: [Make the top level readable on a large PR](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/144) (version A, locked), [Prototype whether the drawn graph and Clusters are one canvas](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/173), [Decide what the PR view's explorers share, and what Clusters needs to ship](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/170) §5–7, 9, 10, [Design the PR view's legend](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/155), [Extend our layout to nested blocks](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/166) (motion, colour, trunks in the legend), [Prototype our own graph layout for large PRs](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/163) (trunk cards), [Decide what the agent must draw in the graph, unchanged parts included](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/156) (lenses, `data`, not confirmed), [the settled brief](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/142#issuecomment-6921640431) ("Settled for rendering", where not superseded). Prototypes: [`canvas.tsx` on `t3/pr-view-one-canvas` (3b97517)](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/blob/3b97517/web/prototype-pr-view/canvas.tsx), the legend on [`t3/pr-view-legend` (592a480, `?key=2`)](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/tree/592a480/web/prototype-pr-view), the nested lab on [`t3/pr-view-nested-layout` (86d3a41)](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/tree/86d3a41/web/prototype-pr-view).

## What's drawn

- **Four columns, left to right:** people and callers; the changed group; the unchanged group; outside (external systems and stores). The changed group sits at the top left, with no empty band above. Each column is a foldable frame: a click on its title folds it into one block.
- **Every top-level part hangs off the system;** there are no grouping nodes. Parts inside a part appear only when it's opened.
- **"Changed"** is the part's own code (settled principle 10). People and outside systems never say "unchanged": they say "person or caller" or "external system", and their panel says "N of its connections are new or changed".
- **A part's face:** kind, change, name, then a bottom line: the change size ("12 files · +1,840 −22") when colouring by change, or the coloured facet's value in words. "double-click ▸" on a part with parts inside, and "partly drawn" beside it for a partly drawn part. No short facet codes.
- **Lines:** one per pair of drawn things at the current opens, carrying all its connections, thicker by count, with the count on the line where it leaves its part when it carries more than one. Arrowheads show direction, at both ends for two-way traffic. **No text labels on any line;** hovering or selecting a line shows what it carries. Dashed: crosses a boundary. **Dotted: not confirmed** (only an undetermined claim backs it). Lines and trunks are purple (`line` and `lineQuiet` tokens): the quiet tone unchanged, the strong tone for added, changed or removed. Trunks draw at 0.45 opacity.
- **Parts with no lines in the current lens are hidden** in a grid behind a "Show N parts with no lines" toggle, counting only the lines the Lines menu shows.
- **Focus:** hovering or selecting a part or line fades everything unrelated to it.

## Opening in place

- **One click selects;** the panel moves to it. A click on the background clears the selection (slice 9 changes this under a purpose).
- **A double-click on a part with parts inside opens it in place:** it becomes a frame titled "▾ ‹path›", its contents grow out of the block's corner and glide into place over 420 ms, and its lines reappear when the glide ends. The clicked block stays still during the glide; then the canvas pans as little as it can to bring the frame's title and as much of the frame as fits into view, eased, with no zoom change. Folding (a click on the frame's title, folding whatever is open inside it) runs it backwards. `prefers-reduced-motion` snaps.
- Inside a frame, a part is named on its own; the frame's title says where it is.
- **A double-click on a line** glides to its far end (eased, zooming out on long flights, the line lit on the way), opening down to it if it's inside a folded block, then selects it.
- **Every element that moves stays mounted, in a fixed DOM order** (an inserted or moved element can't transition).
- **← Back and Start over,** in a bar above the canvas: Back undoes the last open, fold or Fold to groups and says what it undoes ("undoes: opened advagent-v3 › runtime"); Start over returns to the starting state. Selections aren't steps; browser history walks those (slice 7).
- **Fold to groups,** beside − / + / Fit: folds to the four columns (boxes come out folded when a column opens). It's one Back step, and Start over undoes it.
- **Starting state:** layout A, columns open and parts folded. Slice 9 makes the PR's fold plan the start when there are purposes.

## Zoom, pan and keys

- − / + / Fit buttons; Ctrl/Cmd + scroll zooms around the pointer; Space + drag and a drag on the background pan.
- **Keys are touchpoints** in `web/src/keys.ts`, in a new area, `canvas` (the canvas has focus), rebindable on the setup page like every touchpoint: zoom in (+), zoom out (−), reset zoom (0), fit, **out one level** (Backspace: folds the innermost open frame holding the selection and selects it), and Escape (unpins a legend row or closes a trunk card, else clears the selection). Space + drag is fixed.

## The toolbar

Above the canvas, shared with Path (slice 10):
- **Lens:** Modules and services (default), Data flow, External connections, Order of actions (slice 11).
  - *Modules and services:* code parts only, no people, outside systems or stores; every `runtime` line between code parts.
  - *Data flow:* only lines with `data`, arrows in the data's direction ("esg → MySQL: reads pending_messages" points from MySQL to esg); a `both` line has arrowheads at both ends and its hover card splits the two directions.
  - *External connections:* lines that touch an external system, store or person, plus lines crossing a boundary; parts not on a boundary-crossing line are faded.
- **Show:** the whole system (default), the change and what it connects to, or changed parts only.
- **Colour by:** the change (default) or any facet. A part with several values of a multi-valued facet splits its fill into equal vertical stripes, up to 3, then a "+N" stripe. Colour is always paired with words (face, hover card, legend).
- **Boxes,** two slots: **own parts** (Folder by default, the `inside-*` facet, or none) and **outside** (an `outside-*` facet, the required "what it does for this system" one by default, or none). Folder is the parent directory the part's `paths` share, "(root)", or "(several folders)".
- **Outlines:** none (default) or a facet, drawn as up to 3 nested rings in the values' colours, then "+N".
- **Lines menu:** **When** (runtime on, build and test off; runtime can be turned off) and **Kind** (call, data, event, all on), each with the count it draws at this level. Lenses constrain it and show it greyed: Data flow fixes Kind to lines with `data`; the order lens follows its steps' `when`.

## Groups

- **Boxes are drawn inside each column frame,** so a value can appear among changed and among unchanged parts. Neighbours in the same box are bridged into one shape; different boxes never touch; each separate piece is labelled.
- **A part with several values** goes into one **"Shared: N ‹facet›"** box in its column, never copied into each box and never given a main value. Its card shows a chip per value.
- **A box is a foldable frame,** with the same gesture as a column. Folded boxes draw summed lines with counts.
- **The Group panel,** for a selected block that isn't a part (a column, a box, the Shared box, and slice 9's same-kind folds): its name and what groups it, "N parts · N changed", lines to other blocks grouped by neighbour with counts, its members to pick from, and, for a box, each member's placement with its claims (for the Shared box, each member's values with their claims). A folded part gets the part's panel.
- **A boundary** selected from a line's hover card or the reference gets a panel listing what crosses it, with its claims.

## A partly drawn part

- **Folded:** "partly drawn" beside "double-click ▸".
- **Opened:** the frame title reads "▾ sandbox · 3 of 9 folders drawn". After its modules comes one muted, dashed **rest block** that can't be opened: "6 folders not drawn: no line, step, purpose or conflict in this PR reaches them".

## Hover cards

Styled cards in the app's tokens, never native tooltips, placed clear of the pointer:
- **A part:** kind, change badge, name, summary, a change line with a coloured bar, size, "N inside", then **Drawn as**.
- **A line:** each connection with from → to, a change badge, its label, kind, `when`, mode, what it carries (two rows for `both`), boundaries crossed, "not confirmed" where it is, then **Drawn as**: "a line, riding N trunks" (or "a line"), "through the edge of ‹block›" for each frame it crosses, and the key rows for its own style.
- **A trunk:** "N lines share this stretch" and the list. **A click pins the card:** it drags by its head, closes with × or Escape, and hovering a row lights that line's whole route.
- Hovering a part or line that rides a trunk lights its own route through the trunk.

## The legend (the key)

A card floating over the canvas's bottom left, clear of the zoom bar, about 300 px wide, at most about half the canvas's height (it scrolls past that), never taking room from the layout. **Open on a first visit;** × folds it to a "Key" button, remembered per browser. It lists **only the styles the current drawing uses,** recomputed from what the canvas last drew. Each row is a small sample in the real style, its words, and a count of what's drawn in it. **Hovering a row fades everything not drawn in that style; clicking pins it** (until clicked again, another row is clicked, or Escape), and the pinned row stays highlighted.

Sections and rows, in order (rows with nothing drawn are left out):

| Section | Rows |
|---|---|
| **Colour: how the PR changed it** (under Colour by change) | Added · Changed · Changed inside · Removed · Unchanged · No change word: people and outside systems |
| **‹Facet name›** (under Colour by a facet) | one row per value drawn · Stripes: several values · Grey: no value found |
| **Parts** | double-click ▸: has parts inside · Partly drawn: some folders not drawn · Dashed, muted: stands for parts left out · Faded: not on a line that crosses a boundary |
| **Lines** | Quiet purple: unchanged · Strong purple: added, changed or removed · Dashed: crosses a boundary · Dotted: not confirmed · Thicker, with a number: several connections · Arrowheads at both ends: both ways · Trunk: lines sharing a stretch · No labels: hover or select a line |
| **Areas** | Column: ‹its name› · Frame: an open part or group · Box: grouped by ‹facet› · Shared box: parts with several values · Grid: parts with no lines |
| **Outlines: ‹facet›** | one row per value drawn, its sample in that value's colour · +N: more values |

Slices 9 and 11 add their rows by the same rule.

## Colour

- Every colour is a token (`web/src/tokens.stylex.ts`), a `light-dark()` pair. New tokens: `line`, `lineQuiet`, the change colours if the panel's aren't enough, and a categorical set of 12 for facet values.
- **A facet value's colour derives from its facet and value IDs**, so kept IDs keep their colours between analyses: a stable hash of the two IDs picks one of the 12, and a collision within a facet takes the next free one in value-ID order. A migration that renames IDs may change colours (accepted).
- Rows are built by the thousand: parts, lines and chips use `cx.ts` class constants, as the list's rows do.

## Browser perf gates (this slice)

On the 50k stack with the tiled analyses (slice 4), calibrated from a measured run, each with a reason:

| Gate | Measures |
|---|---|
| `browser.pr-cold.ms` | navigation to the frame with the top-level drawing, cold |
| `browser.pr-cold.depth` | round trips chained before the drawing: **2** (shell → chunk ∥ graph), exact |
| `browser.pr-open.ms` | from the PR panel's link in a warm app to the drawing |
| `browser.pr-warm.kb` | a revisit's bytes for the analysis (a `304` and a cached claims file), exact |
| `browser.pr-block-open.ms` and its long tasks | a click on a block to the frame its glide starts in |

When the claims finish arriving isn't gated.

## Tests

Browser, on the recorded analysis and the cases: each lens, Show, Colour by (a multi-valued part's stripes), Boxes (Shared box), Outlines, the Lines menu (counts, greyed under a lens), the no-lines grid; open, fold, Back, Start over, Fold to groups; double-click a line; the partly drawn part's frame and rest block; hover cards (Drawn as); the trunk card pinned, dragged and closed; the legend (rows match what's drawn, hover and pin, folding remembered); the keys and rebinding one; the Group panel. Both themes.

## Done when

The checks pass, the gates are calibrated, and the recorded analysis and the 3× tiled one both draw and open within their budgets.

issues.title: Purposes: the walkthrough, conflicts and the fold plan
issues.body:
Part of [PR view spec](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/174). Build order: **9 of 12**, after "The canvas".

## What this builds

The purpose view, crossing the code view: the panel's **walkthrough** at every place, **Conflicts**, rules, shared causes, unclaimed parts and the fallback, and the canvas's **fold plan** for the PR and each purpose.

Sources: [Stop the boundary-crossings overview flooding on large PRs](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/145), [Prototype the panel's walkthrough of purposes](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/159) (layout A, "Reader"), [Prototype showing a purpose on the canvas](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/160) (B, "Fold the rest"), [Decide the purpose and conflict data the agent produces](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/161), [Decide what the PR view's explorers share, and what Clusters needs to ship](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/170) §8, §10. Prototypes: [`walkthrough.tsx` (6049795, `?wt=A`)](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/blob/6049795e9ebb49491b9bf49aab78925b6b1ed36d/web/prototype-pr-view/walkthrough.tsx) and [`purpose-canvas.tsx` (91bfecc, `?pc=B`)](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/blob/91bfecc057d2a79df6f72a23d9b008bd79105b46/web/prototype-pr-view/purpose-canvas.tsx), with the made-up many-purpose PR from [`make-synthetic.ts`](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/blob/91bfecc057d2a79df6f72a23d9b008bd79105b46/web/prototype-pr-view/make-synthetic.ts).

## The walkthrough

**Where it applies:** the whole PR (nothing selected), a purpose or sub-purpose, a part, a line. A step, a boundary or a group keep their reference panel (slices 7, 8).

**Top, at every place:** a trail back up (PR › purpose › sub-purpose, or the part's parents), a kind line (`The whole PR · 6 purposes`, `Purpose · feature`, `Sub-purpose · groundwork`, `Part · 2 purposes` counting top-level purposes, `Connection`) and the title.

**The walk:** intro, journey and destination as one paragraph, 2–3 sentences in all, never three labelled blocks. A part or line with no written walk gets one built from the code view's one-liners, marked "No walkthrough was written for this; it's built from the code view's one-liners."

**Sources:** chips at the end of the paragraph, one per kind: `PR` (the description), `#N` (an issue) and `code ×n` (counts from the graph, before the claims arrive). A chip opens under the paragraph: description and issue chips show quotes, each saying which claim it backs; code chips show the claim box with its lines. **"Stated, not found in code"** follows the chips in the changed colour, in italics, when any claim behind the paragraph has only stated evidence; hovering it explains: the description or an issue says so, and the analysis found no code that shows it. It marks the whole paragraph (claims are per walk).

**Then, by place, in this order:**
- **A purpose:** **"Rules it sets"** right after the paragraph, when it has rules. Each row: the text, the scope muted, and the result: "Checked 48 handlers: all hold", or "46 hold, 2 break ›" linking the conflict, plus "· 3 not determined". "How it was checked" (`searched`) is folded under the row. A rule that holds gets as much room as one that breaks.
- **A part or line:** **"In this PR's purposes"**, grouped by top-level purpose: one dot and the purpose's name (a link), its sub-purposes under it, each with the role in one line ("(through ‹part›)" when served through a part inside it). A part no purpose passes through: "None: the PR's purposes don't pass through it."
- **A line:** What flows (`data`), When (`occurs`), Needed by (`neededBy`, parts and purposes as links).
- **A part:** **"How it's built"**, rows labelled Decision, Constraint or Assumption (`built`), then **"What it now does"** (`changeSummary`).
- **The next level,** numbered, each row a name and one line: "Its purposes, in order" at the PR; "The journey" at a purpose (its `stops`); "Inside it" at a part; "The connections" at a line. Hovering a row lights it on the canvas; clicking stands on it.
- **At the PR, after the purposes:** "12 changed parts serve no purpose ›" when `unclaimed` isn't empty.
- **Conflicts (n).**
- **The reference, folded at the end:** "All changes, by kind" at the PR, "Questions, facets, files and evidence" everywhere else (slice 7's content).

**Fallback:** when `unbacked` is present, its sentence leads the PR's panel with "All changes, by kind" unfolded under it.

## Conflicts

No verdict anywhere.
- **A card:** header is the question both sides answer, with the kind small on the right ("stated vs code", "purpose vs purpose", "purpose vs code outside the diff"). One row per side: who says it on the left (the purpose's name with its dot, "PR description", "#N", "The code" or "Code outside the diff"), the few-word answer (`says`) on the right.
- **Opening a row** shows the whole fact (`text`) and its source: the quote, or the claim box. A purpose side adds "Go to the purpose ›". A purpose-outside side lists its first 20 sites with evidence, then "and 37 more", with the search that found them.
- **Hovering a card** lights everything it touches.
- **Shared causes:** conflicts with the same `cause` form one card: the cause and its claims as the header, then each question with its two rows. Cause cards come first, then lone conflicts, each in reading order.
- **Which show where:** every conflict at the PR; at a purpose, those touching it or its sub-purposes; at a part, those touching it, a part inside it or a part it sits in; at a line, those touching it.

## Purpose colours

Each top-level purpose has a colour from its place in reading order, over 8 categorical tokens (they repeat after 8); a sub-purpose takes its parent's. The panel shows them as dots (in "Its purposes, in order", the trail, a purpose's title, conflict rows), so the panel is the purpose key. The legend gets one row, "● Dots: the purposes it serves (the panel names them)", when dots are drawn.

## The canvas at a purpose: the fold plan

**Where it applies:** while the panel stands on the whole PR (members: every purpose's parts) or a purpose or sub-purpose (its parts and its sub-purposes'). Picking a part or line inside keeps the canvas as it is. The order lens keeps its own drawing.

**Rolling up to a budget of 16 blocks** (8 on the phone, slice 12):
- Start from the top-level parts holding members. While within budget, open the block holding the most members. The plan is made once per purpose, so later opens never rearrange it.
- If there are still too many blocks, fold siblings of one kind into a single block, largest set first: "middleware in 21 services", with a breakdown line ("store 22 · middleware 21"). Such a block is a group (slice 8's Group panel).
- In each frame, siblings that serve no member fold into one muted, dashed **rest block** that can't be opened: "5 other people", "don't serve it".
- A block says how much of it serves the purpose: "4 of 9 parts serve it".
- A block carries one dot per top-level purpose served by it or a part inside it; the dot of the purpose you stand on is larger.
- The purpose's own lines (`carries`) are drawn strong in its colour, the rest faint. A line between two rest blocks is dropped.
- **Boxes are ignored** under the fold; they return when you leave it.

**Unchanged code reached only through a conflict:** a part no purpose names but a conflict touches (`touches.nodes`) gets its own frame at the top level, "Outside the diff: only through a conflict". Its blocks are dashed, with "unchanged · ⚠ ‹conflict's question›", and their lines to the purpose's blocks are drawn. It shows at the PR, and at a purpose whose conflicts touch it.

**Clicks and history under the fold:**
- One click selects; a double-click opens the block in place, or, on a part with nothing inside, goes to the code view at that part.
- A click on the background goes back to the purpose (or the PR), not to nothing.
- ← Back and Start over (slice 8) work on opens and folds; Start over returns to the purpose's plan. Standing on another purpose starts a fresh Back history. Fold to groups keeps the dots, "N of M parts serve it" and the line strengths, and Start over returns to the plan.

**Into the code view and back:** the canvas header shows the trail (All purposes › ● purpose) and **"Code view at ‹part› ›"** for the selected part. That, or a double-click on a part with nothing inside, leaves the fold: the canvas goes to layout A opened down to that part, selected. A bar then offers **"← Back to ‹purpose›"**, which returns to the folded canvas as it was. Picking the PR or a purpose in the panel also returns.

**Starting state (desktop):** the PR's fold plan when there are purposes; layout A when `unbacked`.

## Unclaimed

Selecting "N changed parts serve no purpose" (`sel=unclaimed`, a history step) acts like a purpose with no colour: the canvas folds to those parts with each `reason` in its hover card, Path's first column lists them (slice 10), and the panel lists each part with its reason.

## Tests

Browser, on the recorded analysis and the cases (sub-purposes, a held and a broken rule, a shared cause, each conflict kind, `unclaimed`, the fallback): the walkthrough at each place with its chips and "Stated, not found in code"; Rules it sets; conflict cards, opening a row, a cause card; the fold plan within 16 blocks on the 3× tiled analysis; rest blocks; Outside the diff; Code view at a part and back; unclaimed; the fallback. Both themes.

## Done when

The checks pass and the recorded analysis reads as a walkthrough from the PR down to a line and back.

issues.title: Path
issues.body:
Part of [PR view spec](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/174). Build order: **10 of 12**, after "Purposes". It can be built alongside slice 11.

## What this builds

**Path**, the PR view's second tab: an explorer of columns of cards, one per pick, that needs no layout engine.

Sources: [Make the top level readable on a large PR](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/144) (variant G), [Prototype whether the drawn graph and Clusters are one canvas](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/173), [Decide what the PR view's explorers share, and what Clusters needs to ship](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/170) §1, §4, §6, §8, [Decide what the agent must draw in the graph, unchanged parts included](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/156) ("Fan-in"). Prototype: variant G on [`t3/pr-view-top-level-variants` (2053e39, `?v=G`)](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/tree/2053e39/web/prototype-pr-view).

## How it works

- **Columns of cards, drawn with lines between them.** The first column is the starting set; each pick adds the next column beside it, holding what the picked card connects to.
- **Columns stay where they are.** Picking in an earlier column cuts back to there, as does the breadcrumb trail above the columns.
- **Each new column starts level with the card it came from,** so the path reads as a staircase of short lines.
- **Explored cards keep a ✓.**
- A card is the canvas's part face (kind, change, name, bottom line, purpose dots), and a line between columns carries the canvas's line style and count.
- **Starting set:** at the PR, the top-level purposes when there are any, else the top-level parts in layout A's order; at a selection, that selection (see "Switching tabs").
- **Stepping through users:** a part's card lists its responsibilities; picking one gives a column of the parts that use it (`uses`), so the reader can step part → responsibility → its users.

## Shared with the canvas

- The selection, lens, Show, Colour by, Boxes, Outlines and Lines menu are one value for the view (slice 7). The panel never changes on a tab switch.
- **Switching to Path** with a selection Path doesn't show restarts Path with that selection as its first column. **Switching to Canvas** with a selection inside a folded block opens down to it (one ← Back step) and scrolls it into view.
- Path's trail is in the URL as `path=a,b,c`.
- **The Lines menu:** Path leaves out hidden lines and ends each column with "N lines hidden by Lines ›" (opening the menu). The no-lines rule counts only the lines shown.
- **"Used by N parts":** hovering a responsibility row in the panel lights its users in Path's current column (and on the canvas).

## Purposes in Path

- **At a purpose,** the first column is its `stops` in walk order, then a folded "N more parts serve it". At the PR it lists the top-level purposes.
- While a purpose is the trail's root, cards carry purpose dots. In each column, neighbours that serve it sort first and their lines take its colour; the rest stay listed, faded.
- Picking a part keeps the purpose as the root.
- **Unclaimed** (`sel=unclaimed`): the first column lists the unclaimed parts.
- A partly drawn part's rest block is a row: "6 folders not drawn".

## The legend

The same key (slice 8), listing only the styles Path's columns draw.

## Tests

Browser: picks adding columns, cutting back by an earlier pick and by the trail, the staircase, ✓; responsibility → users; tab switches both ways with a selection; `path=` restored from a link; Lines hiding with the column note; a purpose as root (stops, dots, faded rest); unclaimed. Both themes.

## Done when

The checks pass and Path walks the recorded analysis from the PR to any part.

issues.title: The order of actions lens
issues.body:
Part of [PR view spec](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/174). Build order: **11 of 12**, after "The canvas". It can be built alongside slices 9 and 10.

## What this builds

The **Order of actions** lens: each scenario as a sequence diagram, folded to chapters, with lifelines rolled up to a zoom level, in two directions.

Sources: [Keep scenarios short enough to follow](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/146), [the settled brief](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/142#issuecomment-6921640431) (principle 6, "Order of actions"), [Design the PR view's legend](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/155) (rule 1), [Decide what the agent must draw in the graph, unchanged parts included](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/156) (`when` on steps). Prototype: [`t3/pr-view-scenarios` (5f76636)](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/tree/5f76636/web/prototype-pr-view), the order lens, `?sq=D` and `?sq=F`.

## The lens

- Choosing Order of actions in the lens picker replaces the canvas's drawing with the sequence view, in the Canvas tab. A scenario picker lists the scenarios by title with their trigger; `scenario` and `chapter` go in the URL.
- **The Lines menu** follows the scenario's steps' `when` (shown greyed): `runtime`, or `build` for a deploy-triggered flow.
- **A step is a selection** (`sel=step:…`); its panel is slice 7's step panel (previous, next, the whole flow).

## Chapters and lifelines

- **A flow opens folded to its chapters.** A folded chapter shows its title (a short sentence of fact) and its step count; opening one shows its steps. Step numbers stay global.
- **Lifelines roll up to a zoom level** the reader picks: top-level parts (default), one level in, two levels in, or as written. Steps that stay inside one lifeline fold into a **"N steps inside"** pill that opens in place.
- **A double-click on a lifeline's head splits it into its children.**

## Two directions, with a switch

"Time runs ↓ / Time runs →":
- **↓ (default on desktop):** parts across the top, steps as horizontal arrows down the page. The usual sequence diagram.
- **→ (the only direction on a phone, slice 12):** parts stacked down a first column that stays pinned while the rest scrolls sideways; each step a vertical line between two part rows with its text beside it.

## Motion

Opening and closing a chapter or pill are animated in both directions: every row or column stays mounted in a fixed order, an opening chapter grows its steps out of itself and what follows slides along, closing runs backwards, about 320 ms, snapping under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Drawing

- Steps are coloured by their change (the change tokens), paired with a word in the hover card.
- **Hover cards** are styled cards like the canvas's (never native tooltips): a step shows from → to, the action, what it carries, its change, `when`, and its line if it names one; a lifeline shows its part's card; a pill lists the steps inside.
- **The legend** lists only what's drawn: Lifeline: a part (or a group of parts at this zoom) · Arrow: a step, coloured by its change · N steps inside: steps within one part, folded · Chapter: one moment of the flow, folded.

## Tests

Browser, on the recorded analysis: scenario picker and URL; chapters folded and opened; the zoom levels and a lifeline split; a pill opened; both directions; hover cards; a step's panel. Both themes.

## Done when

The checks pass and every recorded scenario reads in both directions.

issues.title: The phone and touch
issues.body:
Part of [PR view spec](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/174). Build order: **12 of 12**, last: it reshapes what slices 8–11 built.

## What this builds

The PR view below 720 px, touch at any width, and the WebKit project for the phone specs.

Sources: [Make the PR view's graph navigation work on mobile](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/158), [Extend our layout to nested blocks](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/166) (following a trunk's lines by touch), [Prototype whether the drawn graph and Clusters are one canvas](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/173), [Decide what the PR view's explorers share, and what Clusters needs to ship](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/issues/170) §3, §4, §9. Prototype: [`mobile.tsx` on `t3/pr-view-mobile` (17c0ffa, `?phone=3`)](https://github.com/AdvanGrid/beghu/blob/17c0ffac7dbc12b4341c505b26dd86cd19688fd0/web/prototype-pr-view/mobile.tsx); its README says how to run it on a phone.

## Width and input

- **Below 720 px the phone layout applies.** At 720 px and wider the desktop view is unchanged.
- **Width picks the layout; input picks the gestures.** Touch at desktop width (tablets, touch laptops): tap is click, double-tap (within 350 ms) is double-click, pinch zooms, a long press shows the hover card, and lines get a "which line?" chooser, because they sit closer together than a finger is wide.

## One screen

- **The canvas fills the area under the top bar, starting folded to groups,** with a drawer over it. There are no tabs: Path's column for whatever is picked is the drawer's Elements tab.
- **Top bar:** Back (only when there's somewhere to go back to) and a title naming what the drawer shows: a block, a part, or "Inside ‹part›".

## Map gestures

- One finger drags; two fingers pinch, zooming around the point between them.
- **Tap:** a folded block opens it in place and the drawer shows it; an open block's title folds it, dropping any picks inside; anywhere else in an open block shows that block in the drawer; a part picks it.
- **Double-tap** a part with parts inside to open inside it, as "Open inside" in the drawer does.
- **Placement:** a pick moves to the middle of the map above the drawer at the reader's zoom (zooming in to at least 0.45 if further out). Opening a block zooms so its width fills the map (never below 0.4).
- **Buttons over the map:** Fit, and inside a part "↑ Up to ‹parent›", which goes out one level and picks the part you came from.
- **Lines and trunks are never tapped on the drawing.** Each line is a row in Elements; the chip on the row is the line. Tapping the chip opens the line's details in the Details tab and lights the line's whole route on the map, through every trunk it rides, fading the rest. "Go ›" moves to the far end (desktop's double-click on a line).

## The drawer

- **Heights:** about 150 px, half the screen, nearly full. Drag by the handle or the tabs; a still tap on a tab switches tabs; a tap on the handle toggles between 150 px and half. A pick opens it to at least half.
- **Elements**, at three levels:
  - nothing picked: the blocks, each with its parts, and under **"View"** the lens, Show, Colour by, the Lines menu and Start over. Tapping a block's heading opens it on the map;
  - a block: its parts, its lines to other blocks, and "Fold it on the map";
  - a part: Details and Open inside, then "Uses or sends to" and "Uses it or sends to it" as rows.
  - At a purpose, Elements is Path's first column (its stops).
- **Details:** the desktop panel (walkthrough and reference) for the selection, ending with a folded **"Drawn as"** section holding the hover card's content. A block gets the Group panel (slice 8).
- **Picking on the map keeps the current tab,** so the drawer follows the map in both.

## Purposes

**The map follows the Details tab.** At a purpose it applies the fold plan with a **budget of 8 blocks**. At the PR it starts folded to groups, not in the PR's fold plan (also when `unbacked`).

## Back

Every step is a browser history entry, so the phone's back gesture and the top bar's Back do the same: a pick (map or list), opening or folding a block, Open inside, Up, a jump to Details (a line's chip, a part's Details button), and a purpose fold. Back restores the map's zoom and position. Changing the lens, Show or Lines isn't a step, nor is switching tabs by hand.

## The key

A one-line strip across the top of the map: the change colours, or under another Colour by the most-used values that fit, then "more ▾", which opens the full key over the map. Under a purpose fold it shows the purpose dots.

## Order of actions

The order lens uses only the "time runs →" direction (slice 11).

## Tests

- **A Playwright WebKit project** at a phone's size runs the PR view's phone specs, beside the Chromium ones (in `web/playwright.config.ts`, holding the suite's lock like the other projects).
- Phone specs: start folded to groups; tap to open, fold, pick; double-tap Open inside; Up; line rows, chip, Go ›; drawer heights and tabs; Back through each kind of step, restoring zoom; a purpose fold within 8 blocks; the key strip following Colour by; Drawn as in Details.
- Touch at desktop width: long press, the "which line?" chooser.
- **A manual step on the build's checklist:** a real iPhone (Safari) and Android phone, in both themes.

## Done when

The checks pass and the manual check is done.
